Watch the og demo · Installation guide · Official site · Visual HTML Skills · Plannotator Inbox · Herdr Annotate

# Plannotator Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. **It plugs directly into your agent** through its hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a plan, html, or finishes writing code, the work opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.

Demo: Plan review with Pi
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab.

AI built in: ask AI about anything you're reviewing,
or launch AI reviews that post comments to the diff.

## Annotate HTML Artifacts

## Plannotator Inbox

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. Any other agent reaches it over MCP with `plannotator inbox mcp`, and `plannotator inbox --help` is the guide an agent reads. [Watch the demo](https://plannotator.ai/assets/inbox-film.mp4) · [More on the Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) · [Docs](https://plannotator.ai/docs/reference/inbox/) ## Herdr Annotate: Plannotator in the Terminal

  

[Herdr Annotate](https://github.com/plannotator/herdr-annotate) brings Plannotator-style review to the terminal: annotate terminal text, review whole Markdown documents and your coding agent's replies inside [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), and send the feedback straight back to the agent as its next message. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Droid replies. Annotations are saved in the Plannotator data directory, so terminal reviews and app reviews compound. ``` herdr plugin install plannotator/herdr-annotate ``` Prefer it standalone? [Plannotator TUI](https://github.com/plannotator/plannotator-tui) powers the document review and runs without Herdr: `brew install plannotator/tap/plannotator-tui`. --- ## Commands On Codex, swap the slash commands for `!plannotator …` (e.g. `!plannotator review`) or the `$plannotator-*` skills. ### Annotate ``` /plannotator-annotate README.md # Local markdown file /plannotator-annotate src/ # Browse and annotate files in a folder /plannotator-annotate https://docs.rs/… # Fetch and annotate any URL /plannotator-annotate report.html --render-html # Render HTML as-is instead of converting /plannotator-last # Annotate the agent's last message ``` Need a realistic document to try? Copy the [product requirements document template and filled example](https://docs.plannotator.ai/templates/product-requirements-document) as Markdown. ### Code review ``` /plannotator-review # Review uncommitted changes /plannotator-review # Review a GitHub pull request /plannotator-review # Review a GitLab merge request plannotator review --gitbutler # Review an active GitButler workspace plannotator review --patch-file reading.diff # Review a static caller-supplied unified diff ``` GitButler users can review the whole workspace, one stack, or one branch layer. See the [GitButler workflow guide](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/gitbutler). ### Plan mode No command needed. Plan mode is wired in through each harness's hooks. Any time your agent creates a plan, the markdown review surface opens for you. ### CLI ``` plannotator sessions # List active Plannotator sessions plannotator sessions --open 1 # Reopen a session in the browser plannotator archive # Browse saved plan decisions read-only ``` --- ## Privacy and network behavior Plannotator does not collect usage telemetry or analytics. Plans, diffs, annotations, drafts, history, and configuration stay local by default. Each plan review, annotate, archive, share-portal, and code-review app surface checks GitHub for the latest Plannotator release when it loads. This sends no plan or review content and gives the Plannotator project owner no usage analytics, although GitHub receives an ordinary request. There is currently no opt-out setting for the release check. Local Git code review can also query the configured `origin` with `git ls-remote` to detect the default branch and a stale baseline; it does not send the local diff. That remote query runs when the review opens, when the page loads its diff, when you switch the diff type or base (including the "Diff out of date · Refresh" button), and when you press Fetch — never on a timer, so an idle review page makes no network calls. Turn it off entirely with `plannotator review --no-git-remote-check`, `PLANNOTATOR_GIT_REMOTE_CHECK=0`, or `{ "gitRemoteCheck": false }` in `~/.plannotator/config.json`; the compare target then comes from local refs only and the "behind GitHub" banner never appears. Content leaves the local workflow only when a network feature needs it: - URL annotation fetches the requested site, through Jina Reader by default for public pages or directly when Jina is disabled or unavailable. - GitHub and GitLab review uses your authenticated CLI and Git remote to retrieve PR or MR data. - Ask AI and review agents send the selected question and relevant plan, document, repository, or diff context to your configured provider. When Ask AI is answered by the agent session that opened Plannotator ("Ask this session"), the question goes to that session instead. - Sharing sends the complete link to whoever or whatever service you use to deliver it. Encrypted short links upload ciphertext to the paste service. - Workspaces is a separate hosted product, so the open source app's local-storage model does not apply to content placed there. The [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) documents these boundaries and the hosted website and waitlist data. --- ## Link sharing Open source asynchronous link sharing remains available for compatibility but is moving to deprecated support. Workspaces is the primary direction for team sharing. No removal date has been announced.

Legacy link-sharing demo: room.plannotator.ai

Share a plan with a teammate and they can annotate it themselves. Import their feedback and send it straight back to your agent. **Small markdown shares** are compressed into the URL fragment. The fragment is not included in the browser's request to the share portal, but it is not encrypted. Anyone or any messaging service with the complete link can read the shared content. The portal host still receives ordinary request metadata. **Large markdown and raw HTML shares** use a short-link service. The share payload is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before upload, the server stores only ciphertext, and the key is kept in the URL fragment rather than sent in the paste request. Anyone with the complete link can decrypt it. Hosted pastes expire after 7 days. Same model as [PrivateBin](https://privatebin.info/). The paste service is [self-hostable](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/sharing). Sharing can be disabled entirely with `PLANNOTATOR_SHARE=disabled`. [Workspaces](https://plannotator.ai/workspaces) is the primary path for hosted team collaboration. --- ## Install One installer covers almost every agent. It installs the `plannotator` binary, auto-detects your installed agents, and configures hooks, skills, and slash commands for each: ```bash # macOS / Linux / WSL curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows PowerShell irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer downloads the binary from GitHub Releases. A full install can also contact GitHub for release resolution and agent files, Ataraxy-Labs/sem for the optional `sem` sidecar, and npm for Pi, selected extra skills, or the managed agent-terminal runtime. Pinning `--version` skips only GitHub API release resolution, not the release download. See the [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) for the complete network boundaries. Want just the binary and nothing else? Pass `--minimal` (or export `PLANNOTATOR_MINIMAL=1`) to install only the `plannotator` binary to `~/.local/bin`, skipping every skill, hook, slash command, and per-agent config: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --minimal ``` Then finish the step for your agent: | Agent | After the installer | Details | |---|---|---| | **Amp** | Copy [`plannotator.ts`](apps/amp-plugin/plannotator.ts) into `~/.config/amp/plugins/`, then `plugins: reload`. Workflows live in the command palette. | [README](apps/amp-plugin/README.md) | | **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Pi: `pi update --extensions` (a plain `pi update` updates only Pi). On Claude Code 2.1.287 or newer, plan review, code review and annotate don't make Claude wait: Claude ends its turn and your decision arrives later as a message. Set `PLANNOTATOR_CLAUDE_MOD=0` to go back to the classic flow. Full walkthroughs live in the [installation docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation). ### Uninstall The safe default removes recognized Plannotator-installed components and keeps your local plans, history, drafts, guides, and settings: ```bash plannotator uninstall ``` Use `--purge` for a full removal of known local Plannotator data as well: ```bash plannotator uninstall --purge ``` Purge requires typing `purge` at the prompt and explains that the data is local-only: it is not stored on a Plannotator server and cannot be recovered. For automation, pass `--yes` (or `-y`); non-interactive removal refuses to run without it. Use `--dry-run` to preview recognized work without making changes. Host integrations are always part of uninstall. If a broken or unavailable host prevents safe cleanup, the command names the blocking plugin manager or configuration, gives exact manual cleanup instructions, and stops before deleting the binary. Complete that cleanup and rerun uninstall. These mechanics keep the ordinary confirmation default-negative, make the irreversible outcome require a stronger explicit word, and still give package managers and scripts a conventional non-interactive flag. The command covers the conventional macOS, Linux, WSL, and Windows binary locations; the managed `sem` sidecar and agent-terminal runtime; installer skills, commands, hooks, policies, caches, and recognizable Amp/Kiro files; and detected Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Droid, Pi, and VS Code installations through their host CLIs. Shared JSONC settings are edited surgically, while strict JSON updates preserve the file's indentation, line endings, and trailing-newline style. Custom or unrecognized files, separately installed optional skills, project-local integrations, external plan-save locations, and invalid configs are preserved (malformed host config is a fail-safe error). If cleanup reports an error, the CLI remains available for a safe retry, and its Windows PATH entry is retained or restored when possible. If PATH restoration itself fails, the output gives the full CLI path for retry and asks for manual PATH repair. For safety, purge refuses filesystem roots, the home directory, the shared temporary directory, symlinked data directories, and non-directory data paths. Existing paths are compared by filesystem identity, so case aliases, symlinks, hardlinks, and bind mounts cannot bypass the root/home/ancestor checks. That identity and every containment guard are revalidated after awaited host commands, immediately before the synchronous data-removal block; a replaced data directory is refused without touching either the old or replacement data. If your dedicated data directory is symlinked, point `PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` at its resolved target and retry. Plan review needs no command at all. The next time your agent proposes a plan, it opens in your browser automatically. --- ## How it works ### Plan review ``` Agent calls ExitPlanMode -> PermissionRequest hook fires -> Local server reads plan from hook input -> Browser opens with review UI -> You annotate and approve/deny -> Approve: agent proceeds -> Deny: structured feedback sent to agent -> Agent revises, plan diff shows what changed ``` ### Code review ``` You run /plannotator-review -> git diff captures changes (or PR fetched by URL) -> Browser opens with diff viewer -> Annotate lines, stage/unstage files -> Send feedback: returned to agent session -> Approve: "LGTM" sent ``` --- ## Integrations **VS Code**: Open plans in editor tabs, view diffs inline, add annotations from the editor gutter. Install from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=backnotprop.plannotator-webview). **Obsidian**: Auto-save approved plans to a vault with YAML frontmatter, tags from the plan title, and backlinks for graph connectivity. Configure in Plannotator's Settings panel. **Bear**: Save plans as Bear notes with nested tags and project metadata. **Notion**: Save plans as Markdown child pages under a shared Notion page. Set `NOTION_TOKEN` in the environment that starts Plannotator, then configure the parent page in Settings. **GitHub / GitLab**: Pass any PR or MR URL to `/plannotator-review` and review it with the full diff viewer, annotations, and file tree. --- ## Remote / SSH / devcontainer Plannotator auto-detects SSH sessions and switches to a fixed port. For explicit control: ```bash export PLANNOTATOR_REMOTE=1 export PLANNOTATOR_PORT=9999 # forward this port ``` VS Code devcontainers forward the port automatically (check the Ports tab). For raw SSH, add to `~/.ssh/config`: ``` Host your-server LocalForward 9999 localhost:9999 ``` --- ## Security Every released binary ships with a SHA256 sidecar. The SBOM is intentionally labeled as a release-wide Syft inventory of the monorepo's locked build inputs and dependencies. It is not an exact per-binary runtime inventory: Bun standalone executables do not expose their bundled JavaScript package metadata to Syft. The canonical [installation and verification docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation#pin-or-verify-a-release) cover the existing installer path; the exact new SBOM commands are included below and must be copied to that Mintlify page before the first SBOM-enabled release. The release gate rejects scanner-side ignored matches and treats unknown applicability conservatively as runtime when evaluating CISA KEV and fixable Critical findings. Its explicit Grype configuration, complete JSON results, database status, and repository policy decision remain available as workflow evidence. To verify a released Linux x64 binary, its existing provenance, and the new SBOM evidence directly: ```bash tag=vX.Y.Z version="${tag#v}" mkdir -p /tmp/plannotator-release-verify gh release download "$tag" --repo backnotprop/plannotator \ --pattern 'plannotator-linux-x64*' \ --pattern "plannotator-${version}-release-sbom.cdx.json*" \ --dir /tmp/plannotator-release-verify (cd /tmp/plannotator-release-verify && sha256sum --check plannotator-linux-x64.sha256) (cd /tmp/plannotator-release-verify && sha256sum --check "plannotator-${version}-release-sbom.cdx.json.sha256") gh attestation verify /tmp/plannotator-release-verify/plannotator-linux-x64 \ --repo backnotprop/plannotator --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" \ --signer-workflow backnotprop/plannotator/.github/workflows/release.yml \ --predicate-type https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 gh attestation verify /tmp/plannotator-release-verify/plannotator-linux-x64 \ --repo backnotprop/plannotator --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" \ --signer-workflow backnotprop/plannotator/.github/workflows/release.yml \ --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom ``` These are separate claims over the same artifact digest: provenance identifies its builder/source/workflow, while the CycloneDX predicate describes the release-wide inventory. The release runbook also canonicalizes the downloaded SBOM and attested predicate with `jq -S` and compares them. Can also be set persistently in `~/.plannotator/config.json`: ```json { "verifyAttestation": true } ``` Installer verification remains opt-in and verifies SLSA build provenance; normal installation does not require `gh`. See the [canonical installation docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation#pin-or-verify-a-release) for details. --- ## Configuration Settings are saved in cookies (not localStorage) because each hook invocation runs on a random port. You can also set options through environment variables or `~/.plannotator/config.json`. ### Optional Vim controls Plan and annotate views offer a default-off **Vim controls** profile under **Settings → Vim**. After `l` refines into a semantic level, `j` / `k` move among sibling rows, cells, or inline targets; `h` moves back to the containing target. evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-share Receiving plugin for **DSH Share**, the macOS Share menu integration for DeepSeek Harness. This plugin receives locally queued files, images, text and links, creates a new DeepSeek Harness session, and submits the content to the configured agent. It must be used together with the native **DSHShare.app** share target; installing this plugin alone does not add a macOS Share menu entry. Use the installation scripts and usage guide in the DSH Share repository. The default installation targets the `desktop` profile. Enable **dsh-share** in that profile and restart DeepSeek Harness after updates if needed. Version 0.1.3 uses the native `dsh-share-helper` bundled in **DSHShare.app 0.1.3 / build 9** for its exclusive OS inbox lock. It requires no Python or standalone Node.js installation. Upgrade both the native app and plugin, then restart DSH. Additional consumers stop instead of delivering twice. Disable other receivers before reloading the intended profile, and stop all old 0.1.1 consumers when upgrading. The default helper path is `~/Applications/DSHShare.app/Contents/MacOS/dsh-share-helper`. `DSH_SHARE_HELPER` selects an explicitly supplied executable for nonstandard installations or isolated tests; there is no interpreter fallback. Cleanup and profile JSON updates use the same native executable. Attachments use sequential 64 KiB streaming uploads when supported by DSH, with a 256 MiB file limit. The encoded fallback for older DSH versions is limited to 16 MiB; larger files are preserved as failures. Inline text plus manifest metadata is limited to 1 MiB. Shared data is processed according to your DeepSeek Harness model and tool configuration. The default local inbox is `~/Library/Application Support/DSHShare/inbox`; pending and failed packages can contain the original content and should be kept private. No pending, unconfirmed or failed content expires automatically. The repository's `scripts/cleanup-inbox.sh` previews old acknowledged completion data and requires `--apply` to delete it. Disable all receivers before using it. Ambiguous records are preserved. 本插件是 DSH Share 的 DeepSeek Harness 接收端，必须配合原生 DSHShare.app 使用。安装完成后启用 **dsh-share**；更新后如未生效，重启 DeepSeek Harness。使用方式见项目根目录的 README。 License: MIT. # DSH Share DSH Share is a macOS sharing tool that sends files, images, text and links from other apps on the **same Mac** to the **DeepSeek Harness desktop app** through the system Share menu. Each share creates a new session with the supplied content and starts the configured agent. English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) ## What you can use today - **Finder:** select one or more regular files, then choose **Share → DeepSeek Harness**. - **WeChat for Mac:** use **Other apps → Choose an app on this computer → DeepSeek Harness** when the content offers that option. - Files, images, plain text and URLs exposed through a compatible macOS Share menu are accepted. Files are limited to **256 MiB each**; folders are not supported. - If DeepSeek Harness is closed, the share is saved locally and the app is opened. Pending content can be received after the app and plugin start. The core workflow is implemented and locally verified. The current native app is **0.1.3 / build 9**; the receiving plugin is **0.1.3**. This project is distributed as open-source code through GitHub: the installation scripts build and sign the app locally on your Mac. The default installation does not require a paid Apple Developer membership or notarization credentials. See [compatibility and validation](docs/validation.md) for the tested environments. ## Before installing You need: - macOS **13 or newer**. Testing so far used an **Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 27.0.1**; Intel Macs and other OS versions are not yet verified. - A working DeepSeek Harness desktop installation. The plugin interfaces were tested with **0.2.1-rc.3**. - Xcode or Apple's Command Line Tools for the native build, which defaults to Apple Silicon and local ad-hoc signing. The inbox lock, cleanup command and plugin profile installer use a native executable bundled inside **DSHShare.app**. Installation and everyday use do not require Python or a separately installed Node.js runtime. The compiler is needed for source installation; the installed app uses macOS-provided runtime libraries. Both the macOS share target and the DeepSeek Harness plugin must be installed. ## Install Download and unpack this repository. Open Terminal in the extracted project directory and run: ```bash ./scripts/build-app.sh --install ./scripts/install-plugin.sh ``` The first command installs **DSHShare.app** into `~/Applications` and registers the Share menu entry. The second installs the receiving plugin into the **desktop** profile. Existing native app installations are backed up under the project's ignored `backups/` directory. Then: 1. Open DeepSeek Harness and check that **dsh-share** is enabled in its plugin list. Restart DeepSeek Harness if the plugin has not appeared. 2. In **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → Sharing**, enable **DeepSeek Harness** if needed. 3. Completely quit and reopen source apps that were already running, especially **WeChat**. Use **Command-Q**; closing a window is not sufficient. For a different existing DeepSeek Harness profile, replace only the second command with: ```bash DSH_PROFILE_DIR="$HOME/.dsh/profiles/your-profile" ./scripts/install-plugin.sh ``` Enable this plugin in only one running profile for the shared inbox. An exclusive system lock blocks additional consumers. If another profile owns it, disable that profile's plugin, then reload the intended receiver. When upgrading from plugin 0.1.1, quit all old receivers before starting the updated plugin so an older consumer cannot bypass the lock. ## Use it ### From Finder 1. Select your files and open the **Share** menu. 2. Choose **DeepSeek Harness**, identified by the blue-haired avatar. 3. DeepSeek Harness opens a new session containing your files and any supplied text or links. The agent starts processing it automatically. The session uses your home directory as its default working directory and currently appears under **Ungrouped**. ### From WeChat Open the content's sharing options and choose **Other apps → Choose an app on this computer → DeepSeek Harness**. Available options depend on the content WeChat exposes to macOS; private formats such as mini-program cards or entire chat histories are not guaranteed. **After installing or updating the extension, restart WeChat before trying again if it shows an old icon or forwarding does nothing.** This resolved the locally reported WeChat issue. ### If DeepSeek Harness does not open Open it manually and confirm that **dsh-share** is enabled. The saved share remains in the local inbox until it can be handled. Avoid repeatedly sharing the same item while checking a pending delivery, as each new share creates another session. ## Privacy and local data Sharing submits the content to DeepSeek Harness and starts its agent. Model access, network transmission and tool permissions follow **your DeepSeek Harness configuration**; only share content you intend that agent to process. The native extension hands content over through a local directory and does not need model API keys. This project adds no independent telemetry or analytics service. | Location | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `~/Applications/DSHShare.app` | macOS Share menu target | | `~/Library/Application Support/DSHShare/plugin/dsh-share` | Plugin files installed by the default installer | | `~/Library/Application Support/DSHShare/inbox` | Pending local copies of shares | | `inbox/failed/` | Failed packages and their error details | | `inbox/.receipts/` | Completion metadata | Once a session is opened and acknowledged, its inbox attachment copies are removed. The resulting DeepSeek Harness session and attachments are retained by DeepSeek Harness. Failed packages remain available for diagnosis; do not publish inbox contents or logs containing shared data. **Pending, unconfirmed and failed content never expires automatically.** Attachments are uploaded sequentially in chunks when DeepSeek Harness provides its streaming interface. Older versions without that interface use a bounded fallback limited to **16 MiB per file**; larger files remain in `failed/` with an explanation. DeepSeek Harness may impose additional attachment limits. ### Clean completed data Disable **dsh-share** in all running profiles before cleaning. From the extracted source directory, preview acknowledged completion data older than 30 days: ```bash ./scripts/cleanup-inbox.sh ``` To apply that policy explicitly: ```bash ./scripts/cleanup-inbox.sh --older-than-days 30 --apply ``` Only valid completion receipts and leftover packages with matching, acknowledged delivery state are eligible. Pending shares, accepted shares awaiting confirmation, `failed/` and temporary packages are preserved regardless of age. Ambiguous records are kept. The tool refuses to run while a consumer owns the inbox; it is never scheduled automatically. Use `--inbox "/path/to/inbox"` for a custom inbox. Re-enable the receiving plugin afterwards. ## Common problems | Problem | What to do | | --- | --- | | Missing menu entry or old icon | Enable the extension in System Settings, then completely quit and reopen the source app. For WeChat, use Command-Q. | | Nothing arrives in DeepSeek Harness | Open DeepSeek Harness, enable **dsh-share**, and restart it after installing or updating the plugin. Check the intended profile. | | A directory or a large file fails | Share regular files up to 256 MiB. DSH versions without streaming upload support are limited to 16 MiB; failed content is retained. | | Very long inline text fails | Save it as a file and share the file. Inline text and manifest metadata together are limited to 1 MiB. | | The plugin reports that the inbox is in use | Disable the other receiver, then reload the intended plugin. Do not remove `.consumer.lock`; the system releases ownership when its holder exits. | | The plugin cannot start its native helper | Update the native app with `./scripts/build-app.sh --install`, then install the plugin and restart DSH. Updating only the plugin is insufficient when upgrading from 0.1.2. | | A WeChat item cannot be forwarded | Retry after fully restarting WeChat. If its private card format is not exposed as text, a URL or a file, share the underlying link or saved file instead. | | Installation or system security checks fail | See [signing and installation diagnostics](docs/signing.md). Signing checks and a visible menu entry alone do not prove a working share. | Additional boundaries are listed in [known issues](KNOWN-ISSUES.md). Other source apps, including Safari, Preview and Mail, still need their own compatibility checks. ## Update or stop using it To update, completely quit DeepSeek Harness, run both installation commands from the new source version, then reopen DeepSeek Harness and any already-running source apps. Upgrading to 0.1.3 requires updating **both** DSHShare.app and the plugin: the app now includes the native helper required by the receiver. The plugin installer preserves a private backup of the profile manifest before changing it. To stop receiving shares, disable **dsh-share** in DeepSeek Harness. To remove the macOS share target, run: ```bash ./scripts/build-app.sh --uninstall ``` This removes the native app, not your DeepSeek Harness sessions, plugin files or retained inbox data. Review any pending or failed shares before manually removing their local copies. ## License Source code and documentation are available under [MIT](LICENSE). The avatar artwork is **not included in that MIT grant**; see the [asset notice](apps/DSHShare/Resources/README.md) before reusing it. DSH Share is an independently maintained integration and is not an official DeepSeek Harness distribution.

decision.reason: Held for license scope or repository/package licensing, package or companion artifact mapping. MIT code and documentation, with DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 and macOS 13+ declared in README. The nested native plugin receives local inbox attachments and submits sessions; source installer maps plugin/dsh-share to the profile. It requires DSHShare.app 0.1.3 build 9 and its native lock/profile helper. Swift and installer sources were read, but no built app equivalence was established. The bundled avatar notice explicitly excludes artwork from MIT and supplies no separate open reuse grant. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-vscode-ide

> A VS Code-like workbench for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop) — **Monaco editor core, an independent floating window, and opt-in feature modules**.

[中文文档](README.zh.md)

Not a VS Code port, and it does not load `.vsix` extensions. It brings the part of VS Code people use every day — multi-tab editing, find/replace, diff, quick open, command palette, themes — into DSH, keeps it in a window you can move anywhere, and adds features only when they earn their weight.

## Screenshots

![Workbench: file tree, Monaco editor and an SSH terminal in one floating window](docs/screenshots/workbench.png)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![File explorer following the session workspace](docs/screenshots/explorer.png) | ![Source control and command palette](docs/screenshots/palette.png) |
| ![Diff against HEAD](docs/screenshots/diff.png) | ![SSH terminal built on xterm.js](docs/screenshots/ssh.png) |

![Settings: theme, editor font, theme and icon import, diagnostics](docs/screenshots/settings.png)

## Why another editor plugin?

| | Layout | Editor | Extensibility | Package size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **dsh-vscode-ide** | Floating workbench, never squeezes the conversation | **Monaco** (same core as VS Code) | Built-in modules + public `ctx.vscodeIde` service | ~11 MB |
| `dsh-vscode-mode` | Docked in the right sidebar | Monaco | LSP + SVN + snippets + extension manager | ~27 MB |
| `dsh-ide` / `dsh-workbench` | Right sidebar | CodeMirror | File tree / Git review | 1–3 MB |
| dock family | Dock rail | CodeMirror | Six packages, install what you need | 0.1–1 MB each |

The trade-off: **keep the editing feel (Monaco), drop the weight (extension host / LSP / SVN)** — and never steal width from the conversation panel.

## Features (1.1)

- **Floating workbench** — drag, 8-way resize, maximize with a 44px top safety strip (so you can always reach DSH's own window buttons), geometry remembered
- **Peek mode** — `Ctrl+Alt+Q` hides the workbench so you can read the conversation, press again to return with editor state, scroll position and cursor intact; a draggable floating button does the same with the mouse
- **File explorer** — follows the active session's cwd, lazy directory loading; **remote workspaces go through SFTP**
  automatically. Right-click for new file/folder, rename, delete, copy path and “reveal in file manager”; drag rows
  onto folders (or the empty area for the workspace root) to move them, with edge auto-scroll and a live drop hint;
  `↑`/`↓`/`Enter`/`F2`/`Delete` drive it from the keyboard
- **Monaco editor** — pre-bundled ESM, loaded on demand; one `ITextModel` per file, so switching tabs never loses unsaved work
- **Tabs & breadcrumbs** — single click opens a preview tab (italic) that is replaced by the next one, double click
  pins it, drag to reorder, right-click to close others/to the right/saved; the breadcrumb bar above the editor
  lists siblings and drills into folders
- **Split editor** — “open in split pane” puts a second file on the right with its own tab row and breadcrumbs;
  both panes edit the same model, so changes and undo history stay in sync
- **Problems panel** — `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+M` or the titlebar `⚠` badge lists Monaco diagnostics grouped by file;
  the badge shows a live error/warning count and turns amber when there is something to fix
- **Status bar** — Git branch with ahead/behind, cursor position, language and line endings
- **Save / close** — `Ctrl+S` (temp file + atomic rename), `Ctrl+W`, dirty markers, close confirmation
- **Find & replace** — Monaco's built-in widget (`Ctrl+F`)
- **Quick open / command palette** — `Ctrl+Alt+P` and `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P` (`Ctrl+P` belongs to DSH)
- **Content search & replace** — `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F` opens a floating search panel: search the whole workspace, results grouped per file, click to jump to the line, `⇄` reveals the replace box for a confirmed replace-all, `⋯` adds include/exclude glob filters;
  `git grep` inside repositories, bounded filesystem walk elsewhere (local workspaces only for now)
- **Hot exit** — unsaved buffers are persisted to `localStorage: dsv:drafts.v1` and restored (with dirty markers) after a restart
- **Diff** — against disk, against `HEAD`, or between two files
- **Git** — VS Code-style Source Control (branch row, message box, collapsible staged/changes sections, per-file
  stage/unstage, colour-coded status letters), commit dropdown (staged / all / commit-and-push), discard, push, and a
  **commit graph** with lane lines, ref badges, per-commit file lists and a context menu (copy hash, checkout,
  create branch, revert). Works on remote workspaces too — the commands run on the server over SSH. If the workspace
  root is not a repo, “select repository folder…” lets you point Git at a subdirectory (local and remote)
- **SSH terminal** — xterm.js with a real PTY, multiple sessions. The panel sits **under the editor inside the editor
  column** (VS Code style, file tree keeps the full height): drag the divider to resize, drag all the way down to
  collapse it to a single strip and click/drag that strip to bring it back. A header button can dock it to the right
  side instead, `⫽` shows two sessions side by side, and the content area has a right-click menu (copy / paste /
  select all / clear / rename / close). Connection details are reused from `dsh-remote-ssh` when available; otherwise
  “＋SSH” lets you type host / user / key (or password) directly — first use needs no pre-configured remote workspace.
  With exactly one remembered host (or a remote workspace) “＋SSH” connects immediately; the chooser only appears when
  there are several or none. Passwords are never stored. SSH tabs are marked `远程`, and connecting from a local
  workspace shows a one-time reminder that commands run on the server while the workspace stays local
- **Local PowerShell** — a real ConPTY session (`@homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch`), so `vim`, `top`, colours
  and Tab completion behave like a normal terminal
- **Themes** — follow DSH, built-in One Dark Pro, or **import any VS Code theme JSON** (editor and shell change together)
- **Icons** — built-in Material Icon Theme, or **import any VS Code icon theme** (sprites are generated at build time and lazily loaded)
- **Settings** — editor font / size, word wrap, line numbers, tab width, **terminal font family and size**,
  theme/icon import, host diagnostics; all persisted and applied without reopening tabs
- **Environment probe** — `await __dsv.probe()` (`probe(true)` writes the result to a file)

## Install

> npm publishing is pending (region-restricted signup). Until then use the GitHub release package.

### From GitHub Releases

1. Download `dsh-vscode-ide-1.0.0.tgz` from [Releases](https://github.com/beiryang/dsh-vscode-ide/releases)
2. Extract it and run the bundled installer:

```powershell
tar -xzf dsh-vscode-ide-1.0.0.tgz
cd package
node install.mjs
```

`install.mjs` detects the profile that already contains this plugin and falls back to the default desktop profile;
pass `--profile "<dir>"` to target an explicit profile directory.

3. **Fully quit DSH** (tray icon → Quit) and start it again — the client bundle is loaded only at startup.

### From source (development)

```powershell
npm install
npm run build                     # required: vendor/ and lib/client.js are not committed
node install.mjs
```

### npm (once published)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vscode-ide
```

### Uninstall

```powershell
node install.mjs --remove
```

Removing the plugin keeps its `localStorage` data (window geometry, theme, tabs).

## Usage

- Click **Code Space** in the left sidebar to open/close the workbench (works even if the window was dragged off-screen)
- `Ctrl+Alt+I` toggles the workbench; `Ctrl+Alt+Q` peeks at the conversation; `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F` opens content search
- Floating button: same as `Ctrl+Alt+Q`, draggable, position remembered
- Title bar: `⌕` quick open, `>` command palette, `↻` refresh workspace, `–` minimize to the conversation
  (same as `Ctrl+Alt+Q`), `⤢` maximize, `✕` close
- Settings live in **DSH Settings → Code Space**

Console helpers:

```js
await __dsv.probe()       // environment probe
__dsv.open(); __dsv.close(); __dsv.toggle()
__dsv.layout.resetGeometry()
```

## Architecture

Three layers with an enforced boundary — see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md):

```
kernel/    Workbench kernel: window shell, layout, palette, registry, themes
           (must not import any feature — checked by scripts/check-boundary.mjs)
features/  Feature modules: editor / explorer / git / terminal
           (each ships its own views, commands and styles)
dsh/       DSH slot adapters: sidebar entry, settings section
```

Third-party code can extend the workbench through the public service `ctx.vscodeIde` (contract v1):

```ts
ctx.vscodeIde.registerView({ apiVersion: 1, id, title, region: 'sidebar' | 'main' | 'panel', order, component })
ctx.vscodeIde.registerStatusItem({ apiVersion: 1, id, order, render })
ctx.vscodeIde.registerCommand({ id, title, run })
ctx.vscodeIde.openFile(path)
```

Contributions carrying an unknown `apiVersion` are ignored with a warning instead of breaking the workbench.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| HTTP prefix | `/dsh-vscode-ide/*` |
| Storage | `localStorage: dsv:*` |
| CSS | `--dsv-*` / `.dsv-*` |
| Service | `ctx.vscodeIde` |

## Security

The plugin can read and write files on your machine, therefore:

- HTTP routes accept loopback + same-origin requests only
- Workspace paths are `realpath`-checked and must stay inside the session workspace
- 2 MiB read limit; writes go through temp-file + rename
- Remote workspaces: file access goes over SFTP and is mapped inside the workspace's remote root
- **Theme / icon import** is the single exception: it reads exactly the JSON path you type (plus the SVGs referenced from that JSON's directory) and never writes anything back

## Development

```powershell
npm install          # esbuild, typescript, monaco, xterm, icon assets
npm run build        # boundary check → monaco → xterm → icons → client bundle
npm run smoke        # loads the bundle in Node and asserts apply/inject
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
node install.mjs     # install into the desktop profile
```

Publishing checklist: [docs/PUBLISH.md](docs/PUBLISH.md). Third-party licenses: [THIRD-PARTY.md](THIRD-PARTY.md).

## License

MIT

# DSH Keys Manager

[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-keys-manager)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-339933)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%5E0.2.1--rc.5-0969DA)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns one provider API key into a managed pool.
It extends the Models page rather than replacing it: providers, models, and the
model picker stay where they are; only the API-key source moves behind the
manager.

## What it does

**Pool and routing**

- Several keys per provider, each with an alias and a health state.
- One key pinned to a session, round-robin for new sessions; a failing request
  is retried on its key, then moved to another key.
- Exponential cooldown recovery, capped at seven days.

**Accounts and sign-in**

- Seven pi-ai OAuth providers can join the pool as an account instead of a
  pasted key.
- Two more sign in through the plugin's own bundled clients: Kilo and Z.AI
  Coding Plan.
- Seven companion transport routes for providers the vendored pi-ai cannot
  speak: Cursor, Devin, the two Google routes, Factory Droid, and the two
  GitLab Duo routes.

**Interface**

- A search-driven Keys Manager page on the plugin's own detail page.
- A "managed by Keys Manager" badge inside the existing Models provider cards.
- Extra built-in providers installed as ordinary `llm-pi-ai` routes — 35 of
  them, listed under [Provider coverage](#provider-coverage).

## Quick start

### Install

In the Desktop or Web app, open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `dsh-keys-manager`,
click **Install**, then **Enable now**. This installs the same published package
as the CLI path, already carrying its built bundle.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-keys-manager
```

One install yields both bundles, `dsh-keys-manager` and `llm-omp-transports`;
enable both — the manager owns credentials and routing, the transport the seven
routes' wire protocols. Refresh the Web page afterwards for the browser half.

<details>
<summary>Install from a local checkout</summary>

```sh
git clone https://github.com/btspoony/dsh-keys-manager
cd dsh-keys-manager
pnpm i
dsh plugin --profile web link .
```

`add` installs the published tarball with its built `lib/` and client bundle;
`link .` builds them via `prepare` during `pnpm i`, as does `prepack` when packing.

</details>

## Use it

### Take over a provider and add keys

1. Search for a provider. Open **Plugins → Keys Manager → View** (`Plugins →
   密钥管理 → 查看` in the Chinese locale); the manager renders on the plugin's
   detail page. Existing DSH providers appear first; the plugin also ships the
   curated extra catalog described under [Provider coverage](#provider-coverage).
2. Adopt a provider. For an existing provider the manager imports the
   currently resolved credential, writes a broker reference into the provider
   profile, and leaves the original key in the credential store so release can
   restore it.
3. Add more keys with an alias. Every key is stored in the Harness credential
   store under its own reference; the manager state document never contains a
   key literal.
4. Manage a key from the three-dot menu: rename, pause/resume, delete. A key
   row shows status, last use, and the recovery time while cooling.
5. Tune retry count (1–3), base cooldown, and recovery grace in the settings
   card.

### Accounts and sign-in

Providers that ship a native OAuth sign-in offer two ways to join the pool:
**Add key** stores a static API key, while **Add account** runs the provider's
OAuth sign-in flow and stores the result as an account row in the same pool.
Nine routes join as an **account**: seven through pi-ai's own flows, `kilo` and
`zai` through the plugin's bundled clients (device code, pasted `zcode://`
redirect), which mint a **static** credential renewed only by **Sign in again**.

| Route group | How it joins | Refresh / renew |
|---|---|---|
| 9 OAuth accounts | **Add account** — seven pi-ai flows, two plugin clients | provider-managed for the seven; **Sign in again** for the two static credentials |
| 7 transport routes | **Transport accounts** — one grant per route | see [Transport routes](#transport-routes) |

**API keys form the selection ring** — sticky sessions, round-robin, retry
failover and cooldowns operate across the provider's keys — while **one
projected OAuth grant serves its provider**, and an account row's counters
reflect only that account's own successes and failures. Per-account ranking is
future work. When the projected grant fails, the account cools down and the
pool falls back to its keys, or stops serving on an OAuth-only route until a
manual re-login.

**`muse-code` needs no transport or account row of its own**: the vendored pi-ai
`meta` route (`openai-responses` on `https://api.meta.ai/v1`) serves it, the
agreement check was static, and the first live call is a manual smoke check per
[Known limits](docs/known-limits.md).

### Transport routes

Providers the vendored pi-ai cannot speak are served by the companion
`dsh-llm-omp-transports` component:

- One grant per route, at `llm-omp-transports/<route>` — no key pool and no
  per-account rotation. Sign-in happens in the **Transport accounts** section of
  the Keys Manager page.
- Models are generated from the pinned `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog@18.12.3` table when
  the transport is built, and the clients are unofficial: read the
  [transports package docs](packages/llm-omp/README.md) and its
  [known limits](packages/llm-omp/docs/known-limits.md) before relying on them.

| Route | Sign-in | Refresh | Model rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | browser page + poll | on the credential seam | 123 |
| `devin` | paste the landed callback URL | none — sign in again | 2 |
| `google-gemini-cli` | loopback `8085` + paste fallback | on the credential seam | 7 |
| `google-antigravity` | loopback `51121` + paste fallback | on the credential seam | 22 |
| `factory-droid` | WorkOS device code (URL + user code) | one refresh in a 60 s window, keeps `orgId`/`region` | 62 |
| `gitlab-duo` | PKCE loopback `localhost:8080/callback`, no port fallback, paste fallback | one refresh in a 60 s window | 16 |
| `gitlab-duo-agent` | paste the `vscode://` URL | one refresh, echoes the `vscode` redirect | 1 |

<details>
<summary>Per-route notes</summary>

- **Cursor** — streams text and reasoning and hands tool calls to DSH's tool
  loop; images are refused with a typed error. The client presents Cursor's
  vendor-internal OAuth identity.
- **Devin** — no refresh: a static bearer whose expiry is derived from the token
  (JWT `exp` minus five minutes, else one year), and without a readable expiry
  the row shows `active` with a blank countdown column.
- **Google routes** — both share one generated `lib/omp/google.mjs` artifact yet
  keep separate grants, account rows and catalogs. The grant is
  `{access, refresh, expires, projectId, email?}`; sign-in resolves the Cloud
  project the route bills, and a `legacy-tier` or paid account whose project
  cannot be discovered fails `AUTH_FAILED` until `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (or
  `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`) is set.
- **Factory Droid** — four wires behind one proxy, chosen by model id inside the
  artifact; rows carry no base URL and the account's residency
  (`orgId`/`region`) survives refresh.
- **GitLab Duo pair** — `gitlab-duo`'s direct-access token cache is keyed on the
  GitLab token, so a rotated token misses it; `gitlab-duo-agent` re-seeds a
  workflow per request and replays the transcript rather than resuming a socket.

</details>

### Selection and failure policy

| Mechanism | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Sticky session | The first request of a session selects a key and binds it for that session/provider pair. Later requests reuse it. |
| Round robin | A new session advances the provider cursor and takes the next healthy key. |
| Retry | A failing request is retried on the same key `retryCount` times. Request-shaped failures such as `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` and cancellation never cool a key. |
| Switch | After the retry budget is spent, the failing key is marked cooling, and the session is rebound to another healthy key. When no alternate key exists, the manager delegates to the composition's normal retry/fallback policy. |
| Cooldown | The first failure cools a key for `baseCooldownMs`. A failure while cooling, or within `recoveryGraceMs` after recovery, doubles the next cooldown; a long healthy gap resets the escalation. The hard cap is seven days. |
| Recovery | The key is automatically selectable again when its cooldown expires; no manual reset is required. |

## Configuration & data

Manager metadata lives at:

```text
$DSH_HOME/keys-manager/state.json
```

with owner-only permissions. It contains aliases, credential references,
health counters, session bindings, and provider adoption facts. API key
literals live only in the Harness credential store; an account row follows the
same rule behind its `grantRef`, with only non-sensitive metadata (email,
account id, expiry) in the state. The file is written atomically through a
temporary file and a rename.

Each managed provider profile points its `apiKeyEnv` at a broker reference
such as `KEYSMGR_ZAI_CODING_CN_3FA2C1`. The Host credential layer answers that
reference per request with the session's selected key. The Models page sees
the profile as configured; writing directly to the broker reference is
refused with a pointer to the manager.

<details>
<summary>OAuth2 extension point</summary>

The state shape already distinguishes `kind: "api-key"` from `kind: "oauth"`
and keeps a nullable `oauth` object beside the credential reference. A future
account flow can add records under `keys-manager/<provider>/<key>` without
rewriting existing rows. Providers whose only authentication is OAuth are
reported as unsupported in this version rather than being treated as API-key
providers.

</details>

## Provider coverage

Four groups, one pool:

- **DSH built-in** — routes from the shipped DSH pi-ai catalog. The set follows
  your installed DSH version, so the Models page is the authoritative list; four
  of them are outside single-key pooling (below).
- **Plugin extra built-in** — 35 routes this plugin adds as ordinary
  `llm-pi-ai` routes.
- **OAuth accounts** — 9 routes that join as an account instead of a pasted key:
  seven use pi-ai's own flows, `kilo` and `zai` are signed in by the plugin's
  bundled clients.
- **Transport routes** — 7 routes the vendored pi-ai cannot speak, served by
  `dsh-llm-omp-transports`.

<details>
<summary>Supported — every plugin extra, OAuth account and transport route</summary>

**Plugin extra built-in — 35** — from
[oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)'s provider catalog (MIT):

| Provider | Route id | API key env |

| StepFun | `stepfun` | `STEPFUN_API_KEY` |
| SambaNova | `sambanova` | `SAMBANOVA_API_KEY` |
| Qianfan | `qianfan` | `QIANFAN_API_KEY` |
| GMI Cloud | `gmi-cloud` | `GMI_API_KEY` |
| Synthetic | `synthetic` | `SYNTHETIC_API_KEY` |
| ZenMux | `zenmux` | `ZENMUX_API_KEY` |
| Kilo Gateway | `kilo` | `KILO_API_KEY` |
| NanoGPT | `nanogpt` | `NANO_GPT_API_KEY` |

| AI& | `aiand` | `AIAND_API_KEY` |

| CoreWeave Serverless Inference | `coreweave` | `COREWEAVE_API_KEY` |
| Fire Pass | `firepass` | `FIREPASS_API_KEY` |
| Ollama Cloud | `ollama-cloud` | `OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` |
| Yolo Auto | `yolo-auto` | `YOLO_AUTO_API_KEY` |

Where two variables are listed, either is accepted; the first is the primary.
CoreWeave Serverless Inference also needs `COREWEAVE_PROJECT=<team>/<project>` in
the DSH process environment before it is added.

**OAuth accounts — 9**

| Provider | Route | Sign-in client |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | `anthropic` | pi-ai |
| GitHub Copilot | `github-copilot` | pi-ai |
| Kimi Coding | `kimi-coding` | pi-ai |
| OpenAI Codex | `openai-codex` | pi-ai |
| OpenRouter | `openrouter` | pi-ai |
| Radius | `radius` | pi-ai |
| xAI | `xai` | pi-ai |
| Kilo | `kilo` | plugin bundled client — device code + poll |
| Z.AI Coding Plan | `zai` | plugin bundled client — pasted `zcode://` redirect |

The two plugin-signed credentials are static, tagged `signin:kilo` /
`signin:zai-coding-plan`, and nothing is written to `llm-pi-ai/<provider>`; the
seven pi-ai rows are the provider's own grants. `kilo` is listed twice on
purpose: the same route takes an API key as an extra built-in and an account
through its bundled client.

**Transport routes — 7** — `cursor`, `devin`, `google-gemini-cli`,
`google-antigravity`, `factory-droid`, `gitlab-duo`, `gitlab-duo-agent`; sign-in,
refresh and model detail live in [Transport routes](#transport-routes).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Not pooled — 4 DSH built-ins</summary>

| Provider | Why |
|---|---|
| `amazon-bedrock` | AWS credential chain (profile, IAM keys, ECS/IRSA/EC2), not one API key |
| `cloudflare-ai-gateway` | API key plus a Cloudflare account ID and gateway ID |
| `cloudflare-workers-ai` | API key plus a Cloudflare account ID |
| `openai-codex` | ChatGPT OAuth sign-in only; no API-key credential — usable as an [OAuth account](#accounts-and-sign-in) instead of a key |

</details>

Every other DSH catalog route exposes an API-key credential; a route you declare
yourself in the profile (`自定义` / Custom) is pooled like any built-in.
