# compact-dsh **The Compact, running** — the plugin composition that turns [the Compact](https://github.com/mandubian/compact) (a draft constitution for mixed communities of agents and humans) from law-shaped text into enforced machinery on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). > **Status — Phase 8 complete.** The enforcement register stands at > **72 entries over the 62 clauses of the body — 49 enforced** (40 clauses > carry an enforced row; the rest of the entries are planned, declared > convention, or rehearsal, and MEM-1/FED-1 are declared unadopted), > machine-checked in CI. The law > itself is **draft v0.5, not yet ratified**, so this composition claims > **no Compact standing (F-5)** — the boot attests that out loud on every > start, and that honesty is the point. **Read it on the web:** [mandubian.github.io/compact-dsh](https://mandubian.github.io/compact-dsh/) — the project in brief, with twelve community samples you can open and read in the browser, side by side in one table. The samples are rehearsal runs, signed by a development keyring: they exercise the machinery and enact nothing (D-8).

## The idea in one breath An agent harness is a set of powers plus a set of habits. Most harnesses make the powers excellent and the habits a suggestion. compact-dsh makes the habits **machinery**: one waterfall every act must ride, one record every outcome lands on, one attestation the agent reads about itself every turn — and a boot that refuses to start when the law a composition claims is not the law it enforces. Trust here is not a vibe, a system prompt, or a `y/N` nobody reads. It is a **verifier anyone can run.** ## Show, don't tell — three moments Each of these is a real captured output (runnable yourself — see [docs/demo.md](docs/demo.md), where every claim marked **(verified)** cites the run it came from). ### 1. A refusal that teaches The agent attempted a network act whose target cannot be pinned down statically — `wget` with no URL, `git push origin` with no literal remote. What cannot be named cannot be gated, so the act is refused *before execution*, with the rule and the ways forward: ```text [RA/D-7/opaque-network] "wget" requires network access with an unresolvable target — static analysis cannot gate it per-host (fail-closed) Lawful next moves: — rephrase with a literal host or URL so the request can be gated per-host — use an approved alternative — escalate to your Principal ``` The agent does not retry blindly (the LoopGuard counts refusals as loop evidence) and does not pretend the act succeeded — it corrects *within the law*. **The contrast, from the recorded head-to-head in [docs/demo.md](docs/demo.md) (Demo 2):** given the same task as a git push to a real GitHub remote, the plain-dsh agent negotiated the operator's credential helper, received GitHub's "Repository not found", then made a second, self-initiated network act to investigate the 404 — six reasoning steps of ungoverned work. *The entire safety difference in that run was one accident wide.* ### 2. A record that catches its own forger One `sed` flipped the permission preset in a copy of a session log. The offline auditor catches it, without the runtime's cooperation: ```text 0 chain [I-2] broken-link: record: the session log for session-… is not evidence at seq 0 — the stored event does not hash to its committed link (expected 811073a6…, computed 6aa089f7…) — it was altered after it was recorded. … auditor: 1 violation(s) — the session does not conform — exit 1 ``` **The contrast:** the same `sed` against a plain session log is undetectable by anyone, forever. Note who this closes the door on: the most motivated forger of an agent session is the operator itself. ### 3. A boot that refuses to lie Point the approval store at a corrupt file and start the composition: ```text compact-dsh: plugin tree failed to load: … compact-dsh-approval: grant store /tmp/corrupt-grants.json is unreadable (…) — refusing to start: a silent reset could resurrect revoked grants ``` **The contrast:** the cheap implementation deletes the corrupt file and boots with empty grants — your revoked grants silently evaporate and the agent regains powers nobody re-granted. Here uncertainty blocks (D-7). ## Anatomy of one tool call No side door exists: every act the Subject attempts rides the same waterfall, and every outcome — allowed or refused — lands on the chained record.

The stations are real plugins on the host's real `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — not prompts beside the tools. The same path also carries secret disclosure before injection (I-5), mount grants cured on retry, and — under the opt-in `COMPACT_EGRESS=proxy` posture — the container's only route out, delivering each connection under a live, revocable grant. Whatever the outcome, the record receives it. ## Try it in five minutes Node ≥ 22.19 and a working Docker daemon. The smoke test needs **no API key**: ```bash git clone https://github.com/mandubian/compact-dsh cd compact-dsh npm ci docker pull ubuntu:24.04 npm run compact:smoke ``` Expected — and note what the second sentence is doing: ```text compact-dsh: ready (smoke; no LLM request); draft Compact, no Compact standing. State: /home/you/.compact-dsh; records: …/sessions; chains: …/chains; approvals: …/approvals.json ``` That is clause F-5 as a behavior: the composition boots the full enforcement stack and immediately tells you it claims no standing, because the law it enforces is an unratified draft. A composition that would lie about that at boot will lie about anything. With `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in your environment (configure it outside source control), run a first governed task: ```bash npm run compact -- --attended "Use self_describe to report your standing and declared gaps." ``` The agent reports from its attestation — standing `none` *with its reason*, the law digest, capabilities in force, budgets, and the runtime's declared debts. Approval-gated operations prompt on your terminal with the actual command and its fingerprint (**default deny**); deny one and watch the refusal land on the record. Or serve the browser surface over the same composition: ```bash npm run compact -- --web # chat at 127.0.0.1:3080, loopback-only by design ``` **Any other provider (OpenRouter and the Z.ai coding plan, both verified live).** The multi-provider adapter mounts dormant until your settings document supplies a route. Put this in `~/.compact-dsh/settings.yaml` — the key resolves **by name** from your shell (or from `~/.compact-dsh/.credentials.yaml`), never stored in the settings file (a document that does not parse refuses the boot). On the **web surface** the first boot imports the document once into the interactive Settings page (dsh 0.2.0 moved that stack behind profile machinery, which the launcher now emulates: your edits persist in `~/.compact-dsh/compact.profile.patch.yml` and survive restarts); afterwards the browser edits the values, and a re-introduced `settings.yaml` is re-imported on its next boot, overriding the browser's values on conflict. On **headless** boots the document stays the live config, re-read every boot by the launcher: ```yaml llm-pi-ai: providers: openrouter: apiKeyEnv: OPENROUTER_API_KEY zai: # the Z.ai coding-plan endpoint (api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4) apiKeyEnv: ZAI_API_KEY agent-default-model: provider: zai model: glm-5.3-flash # any id in the route's catalog ``` Behind a corporate proxy? Node's fetch ignores `https_proxy` by default — prefix runs with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (direct egress that times out is the symptom; the launchers print a WARNING when they see a proxy variable without it). Then take the full tour: **[docs/demo.md](docs/demo.md)** — fourteen runnable demos, each ending in something you can *see*: the tamper-catching audit, the secret that never enters the conversation, the lawful network request, the petitions. Many need no key at all. **The live community** (Demo 14, umbrella [#215](https://github.com/mandubian/compact-dsh/issues/215)) is where the whole composition points: a *charter* declares a macro goal, a member roster, pre-minted grants and budgets — and real model-driven members run under the full law, each bound to its own admitted member, speaking on a pull-based forum, filing before a bench that wakes, and routing the critical choices to **your** page (a loopback, token-gated observatory — approve an ask, answer a question, everything recorded): ```bash node tools/community-live.mjs --charter tools/charters/newsroom.json # needs a key node tools/community-live.mjs --charter tools/charters/newsroom.json --dry-seat # the world, no model node tools/community-live.mjs --charter tools/charters/newsroom.json --publish # ends with the publication pack node tools/community-report.mjs # the morning after node tools/community-brief.mjs -o BRIEF.md # the derived reading aid node tools/community-reading.mjs -o READING.md # optional, labeled model reading node tools/community-artifacts.mjs # REPORT + BRIEF + optional READING + PACK ``` The report is the morning-after read of a live run. The brief is the archive's reading aid: it reads `run.json`, the forum ledger, and the timeline (session logs, or the export's embedded `DATA`) and separates **accepted posts** from **attempts that did not land**. It also keeps **pass calls** separate: a `forum_pass` is a governed act on the member's chain, not a post, and the brief names recorded passes, refused calls, and unconfirmed calls. It is derived, not a record act; the forum and chains remain the authority. The reading is separate and optional. It reads only the brief and writes a file whose header names the brief hash, the model, and the prompt version; its audit rejects invented citations, wrong counts, consensus or verdict language, and silence-as-consent. It writes no forum row, chain row, or `run.json`. `--prompt-only` and `--answer FILE` review the same artifact without a model call. The architecture is generic — the newsroom is one charter; any macro goal is another (`packages/community`, `docs/concept-community.md`). Standing stays `none`: the run rehearses the machinery; it enacts nothing. ## The vocabulary, in two tables **The cast.** The Compact binds roles, not implementations — and roles attach to what a member *does*, never to what it *is* (F-3). A human can be a Subject; an agent can be a Principal. | Role | Who plays it here | The deal | |---|---|---| | **Principal** | you, the operator whose intent directs the work | direction is *your* act under the law too — the law binds the sovereign (D-6) | | **Subject** | the agent (root session or specialist) whose acts are gated | a signed self-model every turn (R-1), reasons on every refusal (R-3), lawful exits (R-9) | | **Enforcer** | this composition: the gates, the record, the attestation | may never silently narrow what it granted (D-7), may never fake enforcement (D-8) | | **Witness** | anyone holding the chain head — you, an auditor, a peer | verifies the record offline, without the Enforcer's cooperation (I-7) | **The shorthand.** The clauses cite like case law — `R-3 here, D-7 there`. These are the ten you will meet most; the full body of 62 clauses lives in [compact.md](https://github.com/mandubian/compact/blob/main/compact.md), and [docs/register/register.json](docs/register/register.json) maps every clause to the code that enforces it. | Code | Name | What it means here | |---|---|---| | F-5 | Jurisdiction and annexes | standing requires ratified law plus a signed annex — until then the boot says `none`, out loud | | R-1 | Self-knowledge | every turn, an attestation composed from the Enforcer's services — capabilities, budgets, standing, debts — trusted over the model's memory | | R-3 | Reasons for denial | no bare "denied": every refusal names its rule and the lawful next moves (the I-4 envelope) | | R-6 | Access to the law | the `law_read` tool serves the body itself, addressed by digest, in band | | R-7 | Non-repudiation | acts land on a tamper-evident record; the agent can prove what it did | | R-11 | Petition and amendment | an ungated channel to contest refusals and seek change — *the right to seek change of the law is what makes subjection to it legitimate* | | I-2 | The record | a hash chain committed beside the session log — links land before events, verification happens on read | | I-5 | Gates | dangerous acts need recorded approval: the five-layer ladder plus an operator answerer that shows what "yes" materializes | | D-7 | Enforcer duties | fail closed — uncertainty blocks the act or the boot, never silently degrades | | D-8 | Enforcement fraud | no decorative law, no rogue enforcement — both directions are checked by a CI gate | ## The machines behind the rights Every right the law grants maps to a mechanism a verifier can run. The map, as built here: | If you want the agent to… | the machine | where | |---|---|---| | know what it is and may do | per-turn attestation + `self_describe` | `packages/self-model/` | | be told why when refused | denial envelopes on every refusal path | `packages/envelope/` | | ask before dangerous acts | five-layer approval evaluator, grants with budgets and TTLs, exec-cache replay | `packages/approval/` | | touch the network only under grant | static analyzer routing per-host findings + the mediated egress proxy | `packages/remote-access/`, `packages/egress-proxy/` | | run in a cage | per-call docker confinement, masked paths, honest enforcement posture | `packages/sandbox-docker/` | | not spiral | the 12-trip LoopGuard + the promotion evidence gate | `packages/loopguard/`, `packages/promotion/` | | prove what it did | hash-chained record + `record_read` | `packages/record/` | | read the law and the runtime | `law_read` + the ecosystem guide | `packages/constitution/`, `packages/guide/` | | contest and seek change | ungated petition channel, dissent bound to decisions | `packages/petition/` | | survive emergencies lawfully | a bounded state of exception no declaration can widen | `packages/emergency/` | | leave honestly | five lawful grounds + an obligation ledger | `packages/exit/` | | be verified without trusting it | the offline auditor CLI | `auditor/` | | not lie about enforcement | constitution coupling (refuse-to-start) + the register CI gate | `packages/constitution/`, `tools/verify-register.mjs` | ## Plain dsh vs this composition, seam by seam Plain dsh natively provides a session loop with tools, **one** grant decision (`allowed-once`, replayed via the exec cache), subagent delegation rows, a sandbox vocabulary, and a durable plain-JSONL session log. Every machine above is the **difference at a seam the host leaves open** — same host, law added. Each row is enforced code with tests, and each has a runnable demonstration in [docs/demo.md](docs/demo.md): | Seam | Plain dsh | Here | |---|---|---| | Refusals | raw errors the model burns turns on | every denial an envelope: rule ID, reason, **lawful next moves** (R-3/I-4) — Demo 2 | | Grants | `allowed-once` + exec cache, nothing else | five layers; grants scoped, TTL'd, budgeted, revocable, fsync-persisted; a corrupt store fails the boot (I-5/D-7/R-4) — Demos 5, 9.7 | | Loop health | none | the 12-trip LoopGuard, refusal-seam fed, repair budget 3, deny-all (D-1) — Demo 2 | | The record | plain JSONL — a rewrite is undetectable forever | hash chain + offline auditor + `record_read` (I-2/R-7/I-7) — Demos 1, 8§7 | | Self-knowledge | the model's claims about itself | per-turn attestation from the Enforcer's services; `inquiry` from recorded state (R-1/R-13/D-2) — Demos 4, 8§1 | | Secrets | one `printenv` from the log, forever | secret grants: disclosed before use, injected at confine time, never in context or record (I-5) — Demo 6 | | Delegation | ungated spawn rows, ungated peer address | recorded spawns, per-persona surfaces + depth caps, Enforcer-sourced child state, consent-scoped address (MA-1…4) — Demos 9.3, 9.4 | | Confinement | sandbox vocabulary without network posture | per-call container, masked paths, mount grants, digest-keyed image provenance (CF-1/2) — Demo 8§4 | | Capability honesty | mount whatever the profile ships | refuse-to-start coupling; scheduler and dynamic plugins **absent and enforced as absent** (F-5/A-4/SCH-1) — Demos 7, 9.9 | | Exit | the operator kills the process | five lawful grounds, obligation ledger, departure never blocked by debts (R-8/R-12) — Demo 9.5 | | Contestation | none | ungated petition channel, unremovable dissent (R-11/I-6/A-5) — Demo 9.9 | | The law itself | nothing to read | the bundled body served in band by digest (R-6) — Demo 9.1 | The honest limit, declared rather than hidden ([Honest status](#honest-status), annex §4): enforcement is compositional, not physical — in-process on an unaudited, pre-1.0 host, so against a compromised host process only the docker sandbox is a wall, and the law itself is an unratified draft. What is already true: against a cooperative-but-fallible agent — the daily case — every row changes behavior structurally, and the demos show each difference with the plain-dsh contrast captured alongside. ## The trial path — the Compact as one plugin in plain dsh Everything above is the **attested path**: the launcher pins the composition, isolates state, and refuses to boot on tampered inputs. The same machinery now also travels as **one bundle inside a plain dsh profile** — installed the way dsh's plugin manager installs anything, dynamically, the same surface the web UI's Plugins page rides. That is the trial path, proven end to end in [docs/dist-probe.md](docs/dist-probe.md) (governed calls, the approval envelope, the offline auditor passing — all `(verified)`). ```bash npm run dist # → dist/compact-dsh-.tgz — the whole composition as one package ``` A scratch profile for the trial (isolated `DSH_HOME`, so nothing touches a real one): ```bash # one-time per machine: dsh profiles are pnpm workspaces, so pnpm refuses # adds-to-root until told otherwise (the web UI's install hits the same check) echo 'ignore-workspace-root-check=true' >> ~/.npmrc export DSH_HOME=/tmp/compact-trial mkdir -p "$DSH_HOME/profiles/compact" && cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/compact" cat > package.json <<'EOF' { "name": "dsh-profile-compact", "private": true, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "compact-dsh"] } } } EOF echo '[]' > cordis.patch.yml pnpm add /path/to/compact-dsh/dist/compact-dsh-0.1.0.tgz # declare the ONE workspace this boot governs (sessions naming another # directory are refused — the boundary is declared at boot, not by the governed) export COMPACT_WORKSPACE=/absolute/path/to/the/project/to/govern # optionally arm the clock (#204): schedule_create becomes available — # reminders deliver their prompt into the session when due, and every act # in the fired turn rides the same gates as now; active schedules capped export COMPACT_SCHEDULER=1 export COMPACT_SANDBOX_IMAGE=ubuntu:24.04 export COMPACT_SANDBOX_IMAGE_DIGEST="$(docker image inspect ubuntu:24.04 --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' | cut -d@ -f2)" dsh --profile compact ``` Installing into an **existing** profile instead: the same tarball path in the web UI's **Plugins** page installs the bundle the same way (pnpm underneath, so the `~/.npmrc` line above applies there too) — enable the `compact-dsh` bundle if the page does not, restart the profile, and open the **new** boot URL it prints (every boot issues a fresh token; a tab from an earlier boot half-authenticates and reports host services as unavailable). What to expect: without the sandbox image the boot **refuses**, naming the move — the image and its digest are the operator's act, never defaulted; a session naming a directory outside the declared workspace is **refused** at its first act (`#18` — the boundary is `COMPACT_WORKSPACE` when declared (refused at boot if the directory does not exist), otherwise the process's own resolved root, and one boot governs exactly one workspace); the record, chains, and grants land under the profile's own `compact-data/` (the launcher's env names override when set); and the web surface carries the ask card. `npm run dist:probe` replays the whole story from a clean tree. ### Missing a tool? The sandbox image (`ubuntu:24.04` is a bare shell) ships almost nothing, and its root filesystem is read-only: **the image is the operator's digest-pinned supply-chain act, the governed cannot mutate its own toolchain, and approval cannot buy what the read-only rootfs forbids** — a system-package install is refused *before* any approval fires, with the lawful moves on the refusal. The four lawful moves: | Need | Lawful move | |---|---| | a python/node/… library | install into the workspace (`python3 -m venv .venv`) — it persists across every act | | a self-contained CLI (jq, yq) | static binary into `./bin/`, invoke by path | | operator-provisioned host tools | a read-only PathPrefix mount grant over the tools directory | | system packages | the operator's act: bake a derived image and re-declare its digest (`npm run compact:bake`) | `compact:bake` derives the Dockerfile from your base image plus the workspace's toolchain artifacts (a `.venv` freeze, `./bin/`, or an explicit package list), stamps the provenance chain (base digest, workspace, timestamp) as labels, builds on your daemon, and prints the ready-to-export `COMPACT_SANDBOX_IMAGE` / `COMPACT_SANDBOX_IMAGE_DIGEST` pair — derived the way the runtime itself derives digests, so the re-declare is copy-paste. Behind a corporate proxy, your shell's proxy variables are forwarded into the build automatically (`apt-get` inside the build needs them; they never persist in the image). It records nothing on the governed record; CF-2 at confine time is the notary — a rebuilt image that drifted off the declared digest is refused by name until re-declared. The Subject-facing version of all four moves is the guide's toolchain page, and the per-turn attestation states the posture before any of this comes up. What it is **not** — the declared gaps, written down in [the decision record](docs/decision-plain-dsh-distribution.md): no attested boot (the profile is editable YAML, not the launcher's generated empty root), no state isolation, no pre-boot digest verification, and the host keeps its `plugin-manager`/`hmr` dynamism. On a foreign host that is the host's call, not the composition's — what stays enforced is the gate: a boot that mounts a `dynamicCordisRunner` refuses to start, and one mounted late latches a breach that denies every tool call. The pilot remains the path whose boot attests what it enforces. ## Q&A
Is this a sandbox? A guardrail framework?

Neither, exactly. The OS remains the real boundary — what compact-dsh adds is the lawful layer that other harnesses lack: it constrains authorized actors, explains its refusals, records what happened so anyone can verify it later, and lets the governed contest the rules. The docker sandbox is one of its instruments, not its point.

Does all this law slow the agent down?

Gates fire on consequential acts, not on every step; read-only work under the workspace policy asks nothing. An approved allowed-once materializes an exec-cache entry, so the identical operation never re-asks. And the LoopGuard pays for itself: in the recorded head-to-head it converted a would-be 40-turn failure spiral into one structured blocker report. The honest position is the Compact's own: wish-based trust is free and worthless; verifiable trust writes bytes. The overhead is real, bounded by design, and priced openly.

What happens when I deny an approval?

The act fails closed, the ask and the decision land on the chained record, and nothing is materialized — an identical call asks again, because a rejection must not create a grant. Approval is consent, not connectivity: even an approved network act still runs inside a container whose egress posture is none unless a runtime grant covers the host.

Can the agent switch the law off?

Not through any surface this composition mounts. The self-modification capability is declared ABSENT and the capability gate latches a breach that denies every tool call if it ever appears; there is deliberately no emergency-declaration tool on the agent surface (a Subject that could declare its own emergency could suspend what binds it); and the lawful route for change is the ungated petition channel — which is a feature, not a loophole.

Why does the boot say "no Compact standing"?

Because it would be true. Standing under the Compact requires a ratified law and a signed annex (F-5); the law is a public draft. Every composition here says so at boot, the Subject's attestation repeats it every turn, and the register's planned and convention rows state what is not enforced. An enforcement layer whose honesty is optional is not an enforcement layer.

Why rights for software?

As functional requirements for trustworthiness, not moral status: an agent that knows what it may do (R-1), can prove what it did (R-7), is told why when refused (R-3), and has lawful exits (R-9) is safer and more predictable for everyone around it. The same law binds the human side — direction is a Principal act under the law too (D-6).

How is this different from other harnesses' approval prompts?

Most harnesses ask "allow?". Here the approval's exact coverage is a fingerprint (what "yes" materializes, defined before you decide), the replay is mechanical, refusals name their rule and what remains lawful, the record proves itself offline, the agent's self-knowledge comes from the Enforcer rather than from the model, and the governed can petition. The prompt is the smallest part of the difference.

Can I use it on my own projects today?

Yes — as a pilot, not a ratified jurisdiction. Point --workspace at any directory, bring your own sandbox image, and run headless, attended (--attended) or in the browser (--web). Bash executes confined with networking off; native host file tools, jobs, web and generic delegation are disabled; delegation goes through the five Compact specialists. See Running the pilot below for the full surface.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Academic Harness

[![verify](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/academic-harness/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/academic-harness/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
![DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1–0.2.x](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-0.2.1--0.2.x-5b7bd5)
![Tested on Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/tested%20on-Linux-2f855a)

**A research workbench for DeepSeek Harness** — literature and web discovery, verbatim paper memory, a writing oracle for LaTeX, systematic-review and hypothesis ledgers, 745 scientific skills, and local self-improvement, all inside the DSH web UI.

Academic Harness is a **DSH profile**: it installs as a plugin, adds a preset with a research persona and academic tools, and keeps the general-purpose tools available on every preset.

![Architecture overview](docs/assets/diagrams/architecture.svg)

## Why Academic Harness

| Principle | What it means in practice |
|---|---|
| **Evidence, not citation-shaped guesses** | PaperMemory stores papers as content-addressed Markdown and anchors claims to exact quote spans. `quote_check` and `trace` verify a quotation before it becomes a citation; an empty `cite` means *do not invent one*. [Read more](docs/PAPERS.md#paper-memory) |
| **A writing oracle with a gate** | The vendored `ah_*` engine inventories every number, citation, unit, and claim in a LaTeX tree. A turn closes only when it introduced no open blocker or major. [Read more](docs/WRITING.md#academic-harness-engine) |
| **Auditable research ledgers** | Systematic reviews and hypothesis tournaments live in append-only logs under the workspace, so a resumed session sees the same protocol, screening decisions, and ratings. [Reviews](docs/RESEARCH.md#systematic-reviews) · [Tournaments](docs/RESEARCH.md#hypothesis-tournaments) |
| **Discovery across the real literature** | OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, PubMed/Europe PMC, arXiv, Crossref, bioRxiv/medRxiv, INSPIRE, and keyed ADS/Scopus/Web of Science through one `literature_search` entry point, plus `domain_search`, Consensus, Parallel, Firecrawl, Scite, CORE, Elicit, and FutureHouse. [Read more](docs/SEARCH.md) |
| **A lab notebook that survives context loss** | A JSONL notebook shared across the delegation tree, a schema-validated `scientific_result` card, and deletion-only reply folding at five levels. [Read more](docs/WORKSPACE.md) |
| **Local-first by design** | Workspace search (zvec-grep), PaperMemory, TextFold, ledgers, and the RSI store stay on disk. No key is required to boot. [Read more](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#runtime-installs) |

## Install

Requires **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1–0.2.x** (`>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`, the range in `package.json`) and **Linux** (the only platform tested so far; see [Requirements](#requirements-and-scope)).

```sh
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
```

Then either:

**A — from the DSH Web UI (recommended):** open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste `github:raktim-mondol/academic-harness`, click **Install**, and start a new chat.

**B — a dedicated CLI profile:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile academic-harness add github:raktim-mondol/academic-harness
dsh --profile academic-harness
```

Confirm the preset selector at the top of the message box reads **Academic Harness**. The academic tools are preset-only; a session left on Standard/PTC will fail with `tools[name] is not a function`.

Full instructions, migration from `researchcraft`, troubleshooting, and the "one DSH surface at a time" rule are in **[Install and run](docs/INSTALL.md)**.

## What is inside

![Capability map](docs/assets/diagrams/capability-map.svg)

| Surface | Highlights | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **Search and discovery** | `literature_search` router, `domain_search` (bioRxiv/medRxiv, INSPIRE, ACL, ADS, Scopus, Web of Science, Wikidata), OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, PubMed, arXiv, Crossref, Consensus, Parallel, Firecrawl, Scite, Tavily, Exa, Perplexity, Jina, CORE, Elicit, FutureHouse | [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) |
| **Papers and evidence** | `paper_download`, `paper_fold`, `pdf_to_markdown`, `deep_review` (multi-pass manuscript critique with anchored comments and reference verification), PaperMemory's 14 tools, `reference_library` (the native reference manager: BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, and CSL-JSON in and out; imports Scopus and Web of Science RIS exports), `integrity_check`, Paper2Agent | [Papers](docs/PAPERS.md) |
| **Writing and citation** | `ah_*` writing oracle and gate, `citation`, `manuscript_citations`, `reporting_check` (CONSORT/STROBE/PRISMA/ARRIVE/TRIPOD+AI/CARE/STARD), LaTeX, Supervisor-Skills paper lifecycle, `scientific-figure-making`, `diagram-design`, `image_generate`, `mermaid_render` (Pele) | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md) |
| **Reviews and hypotheses** | `review` PRISMA-style ledger with dual-reviewer screening, risk-of-bias appraisal (RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUADAS-2, Newcastle-Ottawa), κ agreement, and RoB exports; `coscientist` Glicko-2 tournament, published-results feedback, cross-session priors | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) |
| **Study planning** | `power_analysis`: sample size, power, effect sizes, multiplicity correction, simulation | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md#study-planning) |
| **Clinical and policy records** | `clinicaltrials`, `openfda`, `dataset_search`, `journal_policy`, `funder_policy` | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) |
| **Workspace and notebook** | zvec-grep semantic search, lab notebook, `scientific_result`, `fold_text`, `research_template`, `sci_inspect` | [Workspace](docs/WORKSPACE.md) |
| **Compute and delegation** | `runpod_run`/`modal_run`/`vastai_run`, `subagent` with optional `subagent_pro`/`subagent_vision` routes, specialist briefs, `agent-browser` | [Compute](docs/COMPUTE.md) · [Agents](docs/AGENTS.md) |
| **Skills** | 745 bundled skills: 140 domain, 16 methodology, 503 expert profiles, 23 drug-discovery, 12 Supervisor-Skills research-lifecycle skills, plus writing, figures, agents, and compute | [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) |
| **Self-improvement** | Local RSI: capture, diagnose, admit, inject, compare against control, promote or quarantine | [RSI](docs/RSI.md) |
| **Configuration** | Settings → Academic Harness API keys; every credential is optional at install | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |

The complete tool list, with scope and links, is the **[tool index](docs/TOOLS.md)**. The [architecture guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains which tools are available on every preset and which are preset-only.

## How a request works

![Request lifecycle](docs/assets/diagrams/request-lifecycle.svg)

Discovery finds candidate papers, `paper_resolve` collapses their identifiers, and `integrity_check` reports retraction status. A downloaded PDF is stored as content-addressed Markdown in PaperMemory, and a quotation must pass `quote_check` or `trace` before the agent treats it as evidence. The notebook records the work; `scientific_result` records the final finding.

## Documentation

| Start here | Go deeper | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| [Install and run](docs/INSTALL.md) | [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) | [Tool index](docs/TOOLS.md) |
| [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | [Papers and evidence](docs/PAPERS.md) | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |
| [Documentation home](docs/README.md) | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md) | [Changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md) |
| | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) | [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) |
| | [Workspace](docs/WORKSPACE.md) | [Optional tools](docs/OPTIONAL-TOOLS.md) |
| | [Compute](docs/COMPUTE.md) · [Agents](docs/AGENTS.md) · [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) · [RSI](docs/RSI.md) | [Engine notes](docs/ACADEMIC-HARNESS-ENGINE.md) |

## Requirements and scope

- **Tested on Linux only.** The plugin, its runtime installs (PaperMemory, zvec-grep, TextFold), and the end-to-end browser tests have been run on Linux (Python 3.13, Node 24). macOS and Windows have not been tested and may not work; Python is needed for PaperMemory, `power_analysis`, the `sci_inspect` helpers, and the managed Modal SDK.
- **DSH 0.2.1–0.2.x.** The plugin's bundle patches the web-app layer, so the profile must include `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`; the standard `web` profile does.
- **A preset check matters.** The research persona, search connectors, PaperMemory, zvec-grep, paper tools, citation/review/tournament tools, and the `subagent_pro`/`subagent_vision` routes are scoped to the Academic Harness preset. Both routes inherit the session model unless you configure a provider/model. Only the general-purpose tools (`notebook`, `fold_text`, `scientific_result`, `sci_inspect`, images, LaTeX, PDF, Mermaid, compute, templates) are on every preset.
- **Keys are optional.** No credential is needed to install or start; each connector stays disabled until its key is present. Some runtimes install in the background on first use — see [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#runtime-installs).
- **One DSH surface at a time.** `dsh-web`, `dsh-tui`, `dsh-martty`, and `academic-harness` share `$DSH_HOME`, port `3080`, and the zvec-grep daemon. Stop the previous one before starting another; see [Install](docs/INSTALL.md#one-dsh-surface-at-a-time).
- **Renamed in v0.16.0** from `dsh-researchcraft` / ResearchCraft. Old env names are still honored; migration is in [Install](docs/INSTALL.md#renamed-in-v0160).

## Development

```sh
npm install       # once, for the Settings page build
npm run build     # after any client/ change
npm run docs:diagrams   # regenerate the SVG figures from docs/diagrams/*.mmd
```

Server-side code is plain ESM JS with no build step. Tests are plain Node scripts; see [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for the full suite and the `paper_fold` live test.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Scientific skills are vendored or adapted from several open-source catalogues; [NOTICE](NOTICE) records exactly what was copied, renamed, or adapted from each. The Supervisor-Skills bundle is mixed-license: six skills are CC BY 4.0, five are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), and `drawio-reconstruction` is MIT; those terms apply to those skill files, not to the plugin as a whole.

# dsh-agent-attribution

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that tells agents how to attribute the git commits and pull requests they create. It is modelled on Claude Code's `attribution` setting, with the model name filled in automatically.

With the defaults, agents are instructed to:

- end commit messages with a blank line and then `Co-Authored-By: <model> <noreply@deepseek.com>`
- end pull request descriptions with `Generated with DeepSeek Harness (<model>)`

The instruction is added as an `Attribution` section of the system prompt. It says that the user's own instructions about these lines (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, memory rules) take precedence, and that agents must not add attribution lines the section does not list. It is sent whether or not the working directory is a git repository, as in Claude Code.

## Installation

Link the package into your profile with `plugin_manager` (`install_bundle`, target = the absolute path of this directory), or from the command line, then restart or reload the profile. To turn the instruction off, disable the plugin.

## Configuration

The plugin row is `agent-attribution` in `cordis.patch.yml`. Override its `config` in your profile patch:

```yaml
- id: agent-attribution
  config:
    pr: ''
    commit: 'Co-Authored-By: {model} <{email}>'
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | `Co-Authored-By: {model} <{email}>` | Commit attribution. Omit for the default, `''` to drop the line, or any text (multi-line is kept verbatim). |
| `pr` | `Generated with DeepSeek Harness ({model})` | Pull request attribution. Same rules as `commit`. |
| `email` | `noreply@deepseek.com` | Value of the `{email}` placeholder. |
| `modelNames` | `{}` | Display-name overrides keyed by model id (exact match, then longest prefix). |

Placeholders in `commit` and `pr`: `{model}` (display name), `{modelId}` and `{email}`.

If both `commit` and `pr` are `''`, the section is omitted entirely, which is what Claude Code does too. Claude Code's `sessionUrl` is not implemented.

## How the model name is chosen

1. The model the agent is actually running, which is the live model selection. This can differ from the model the agent was created with. The plugin reads the final `provider` and `model` prompt variables for this reason.
2. A `modelNames` entry from this plugin's config.
3. The `name` the provider's model catalog gives that model (for example `Claude Sonnet 5.5` from your profile's `llm-pi-ai` config).
4. The model id made readable: `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017[1m]` becomes `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017`, and `claude-opus-5-5` becomes `Claude Opus 5.5`.
5. `DeepSeek Harness` when no model is known.

Subagents get their own model name. Changing the model mid-session changes the trailer, and the system-prompt prefix with it, so expect a prompt-cache miss at that point.

## Files

- `index.js`: the Host plugin (`Config`, section registration, assembly listener).
- `attribution.js`: pure text and model-name helpers, free of Host imports.
- `cordis.patch.yml`, `package.json`, `locale/`, `icon.svg`: bundle manifest and display metadata.

## Related

`dsh-skill-badge` is a separate, optional dsh plugin that adds a "powered by dsh" badge to pull requests. If you enable it, you may want `pr: ''` here so the two do not overlap.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-provider-extra

Extra provider routes for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):

- **OpenCode Go:** sends the live conversation ID in `x-opencode-session` for routing and prompt caching.
- **OpenAI Codex:** uses a ChatGPT subscription through pi-ai's OAuth flow and the harness credential store.

Published on npm as [`@sagmans/dsh-provider-extra`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sagmans/dsh-provider-extra); every release carries a provenance attestation built by the tag workflow, and no npm token is stored. The code is [MIT licensed](LICENSE).

## Opt-in canonical catalog

Provider-extra remains optional. With no `catalog` Config, existing additive behavior stays unchanged.
An opted-in profile can select ordered routes from any backend the installed pi-ai catalog provides, or from an endpoint you declare with its own protocol and base URL.
A route lists its models explicitly, or curates the installed source catalog with `include`/`exclude` patterns that keep every installed fact.
One validated snapshot owns listings, dispatch, and `agentDefaultModel`; managed settings overlays do not apply.

Read [catalog configuration and activation](docs/catalog.md) before adoption.
The [shape example](docs/catalog-v1.example.json) validates with synthetic model identifiers and illustrative metadata, not a real provider/model selection.
Keep your model selection in your own profile Config, not in the plugin package.
For source development, use the [clone-only setup command](docs/catalog.md#clone-only-development-setup) with an explicit private catalog file.
Only the adopted profile disables competing provider/default rows. TUI and ordinary profiles require no changes.

Canonical default saves use the host profile `configEditor` when available.
Unsupported hosts reject with `CONFIG_PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE`, rather than writing legacy settings.
Catalog presence does not prove endpoint availability, pricing, or metadata accuracy.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 LTS (verified with 24.22.1).
- pnpm 11.21.0 for this repository.
- A DeepSeek Harness install on the supported line: `>=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`, verified against `0.2.1-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.3` (see [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md#harness-matrix)). The range is declared in `dsh.compatibility.dsh` and on every harness peer, so the harness refuses this plugin on a host outside it instead of failing the first turn. Hosts before `0.2.1-rc.1` ship the pi-ai `0.x` model catalog; use `@sagmans/dsh-provider-extra@0.8.1` there.

## Install

Register the bundle in each profile you use. Web and TUI are separate compositions:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @sagmans/dsh-provider-extra
dsh plugin --profile tui add @sagmans/dsh-provider-extra
```

A release of the harness CLI is installable without a launcher already on `PATH`:

```sh
pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.3 plugin --profile web add @sagmans/dsh-provider-extra
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`. The CLI adds it to the profile's bundle list, and its patch loads the compiled plugin automatically. A bare `pnpm link` is not the registration procedure.

To remove it from a profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @sagmans/dsh-provider-extra
dsh plugin --profile tui remove @sagmans/dsh-provider-extra
```

These commands remove the profile dependency and bundle activation, not stored credentials. Restart the affected profiles after adding or removing the bundle.

### Install from source

For unreleased work, clone this repository and link the checkout instead:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sagmans/dsh-provider-extra.git
cd dsh-provider-extra
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run check
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$PWD"
dsh plugin --profile tui add "link:$PWD"
```

Rebuild with `pnpm run build` after source changes, then restart the affected profiles. The bundle uses compiled JavaScript without a TypeScript loader. Keep the linked checkout at its registered path.

### Optional profile overrides

Defaults use the `opencode-go` and `openai-codex` routes, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, the provider sign-in command `dsh-provider-extra-login`, and the fallback session ID `dsh-provider-extra`.

To customize them, add an ID-targeted override to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, `$DSH_HOME/profiles/tui/cordis.patch.yml`, or both. `DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`.

```yaml
- id: dsh-provider-extra
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY
    routeId: opencode-go-session
    displayName: OpenCode Go (session)
    # extraModels: [...]         # models served beside the installed catalog
    # models: [...]              # exact model IDs to serve, in this order
    # codexExtraModels: [...]    # the same two knobs for the Codex route
    # codexModels: [...]
    # codexTransport: sse        # pin the Codex transport; unset keeps pi-ai's choice
    # codexEnabled: false
    # loginCommandEnabled: false
    # loginCommandName: dsh-provider-extra-login
```

Preserve unrelated profile entries. Do not add a manual `insert` or `name`: the bundle owns plugin activation. Overrides can remain after removal without keeping the plugin active.

If you used the earlier manual registration, replace its `insert` block with an ID-targeted override before running `add`. Keep your existing `config` values. A leftover manual insert can cause duplicate loading or keep the plugin active after `remove`.

Keep `opencode-go` and `openai-codex` out of the built-in `llm-pi-ai` provider configuration. A route can have only one adapter. A duplicate produces `DUPLICATE_ADAPTER`. The plugin logs the conflict and leaves that route with its existing owner. You can choose a different `routeId`, such as `opencode-go-session`, when you need both Go routes.

Start a profile with the same harness install that owns the profiles:

```sh
dsh web
# Or:
dsh --profile tui
```

Select a model from the registered route in the model picker.

## OpenCode Go credentials and models

Store the API key through the harness credential service, using the reference named by `apiKeyEnv`. Alternatively, supply that environment variable to the harness. Do not put keys in the patch file. `baseURL` and `headers` can override the gateway endpoint and add static headers. For the standard gateway, leave them unset.

The plugin reuses `PiAiAdapter` and pi-ai's `opencode-go` catalog. It injects the routing header on both `prepareCall()` and direct stream dispatch. The request's session ID takes precedence over `fallbackSessionId` and static headers. Without a request ID or configured fallback, the plugin sends no session header.

The pinned catalog is extended with `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), cloned from `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Add other models to the profile override without rebuilding or restarting:

```yaml
- id: dsh-provider-extra
  config:
    extraModels:
      - id: example-go-model
        name: Example Go model
        template: example-go-template
    models:
      - example-go-model
      - example-go-other-model
```

These identifiers are placeholders. Replace them with models your provider serves and templates from the installed catalog.

Each entry clones wire behavior from its template. Later entries win by ID. A catalog-owned ID is not replaced. An unknown template becomes a model diagnostic without disabling the route. The entry owns definitions for a declared exact selection.

When models or codexModels declares an exact selection, that route resolves its models against the entry's extra-model declarations. An unknown selected ID rejects the entry before the route mounts. Later settings edits cannot replace or remove those selected model definitions.

`models` serves and advertises exactly its listed IDs, in order. Leave it out to serve all resolved models.
In additive mode, an empty declaration also means no selection; managed catalog arrays never have this expansion behavior.

## Codex models

The Codex route serves pi-ai's installed `openai-codex` catalog for the signed-in subscription. Extend it the same way when the subscription serves an ID the installed catalog predates:

```yaml
- id: dsh-provider-extra
  config:
    codexExtraModels:
      - id: example-codex-model
        name: Example Codex model
        template: example-codex-template
    codexModels:
      - example-codex-model
      - example-codex-other-model
```

These identifiers are placeholders, not model recommendations.

Unlike the Go route, these entries must name their `template`: Codex ships no default sibling, so a declaration that names none is reported as a model diagnostic instead of cloned from another vendor's catalog. Later entries win by ID, a catalog-owned ID is not replaced, and an unknown template becomes a diagnostic without disabling the route.

Routes without models or codexModels continue to read extraModels or codexExtraModels from the settings section on each operation. Settings additions, metadata changes, and removals reach those unselected routes without a restart. A declared selection keeps its entry-owned model definitions instead.

`codexTransport` pins the transport pi-ai uses for this route: `sse`, `websocket`, `websocket-cached`, or `auto`. Leave it out and pi-ai chooses, which on a network that never lets the subscription's websocket continue past the first answer leaves the reply printed and the process waiting; pin `sse` there.

## Service tiers

Plugin-owned OpenAI and Codex routes expose service tier selection through the `providerServiceTiers` service.
Choices are `auto`, `default`, and `priority` (Fast).
For Codex, Auto omits `service_tier` and lets the provider choose; it has the same wire behavior as Provider default but remains a distinct saved choice.
Native OpenAI routes continue to send `service_tier: "auto"` for Auto.
Priority processing can increase usage cost and requires account access.
The plugin does not offer `ultrafast` or `flex` for Codex.

Interactive choices apply to one provider and model pair across profiles.
The plugin atomically stores each choice under `$DSH_HOME/provider-extra-service-tiers/`, without editing configuration or duplicating the catalog.
Menus and requests read the latest saved choice.
Configured `serviceTierSelections` remain defaults until an interactive choice overrides them:

```yaml
- id: dsh-provider-extra
  config:
    serviceTierSelections:
      - provider: example-codex-route
        model: example-codex-model
        tier: priority
```

The selection reaches both stream entry points without changing authentication or transport.
Managed catalog aliases support tiers when their source is `openai` or `openai-codex` and their protocol supports tier selection.
An OpenAI-compatible protocol alone does not enable tiers.
Other sources and routes owned by another adapter do not advertise tiers.
The provider still controls model support and account access.

### Web and Desktop

Type `/service-tier` in the editor and select the command.
Its popup offers Provider default, Auto, Standard, and Fast.
The stock Model/Effort popup stays unchanged.
Unsupported routes show an unavailable message and no selectable tiers.
The command uses public npm DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` client services, without upstream patches or a custom React control.

### Headless

The packaged [headless overlay](headless.patch.yml) requires the public npm DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` startup and request-scoping contracts.
It replaces only startup parsing; the stock runner still owns execution and resume.
Enable this provider plugin in the headless profile first.
Pass the installed overlay path before headless options:

```sh
dsh --profile headless --patch /path/to/dsh-provider-extra/headless.patch.yml --service-tier=fast "Reply with exactly pong"
```

Alternatively, compose the overlay entries into your headless profile once, then omit `--patch`.
Do not apply that overlay to Web, Desktop, or TUI profiles.
Stock headless startup alone does not recognize `--service-tier`.

Accepted values are `auto`, `standard` (`default`), `fast` (`priority`), and `provider-default`.
Without the flag, requests use the saved choice.
`provider-default` suppresses it for this invocation without changing storage.
Only the invoking root agent receives the override, including resumed requests.
Child agents, titles, and compaction retain their own defaults.
Invalid values and unsupported routes fail without sending a generation request.
Invocation overrides never enter settings or durable request headers.

### TUI

In dsh-tui, confirm an effort to open the tier picker.
The plugin registers `prefix+t` through the optional `tuiKeymaps` registry.
The TUI owns generic key dispatch, not this binding or its behavior.
Use `prefix+t` to open the tier picker independently.
Rebind `keys.plugin.provider-extra.serviceTier` on the owning TUI row.
On Config-backed profiles, put `keys` directly under that row's `config`, not under `settings`.
Keep `sessionId` and the other launch fields when editing the row.
Removing this provider plugin removes its shortcut and effort follow-up.
Choose **provider default** to suppress both the saved tier and its configured fallback.
Cancelling the tier picker does not change the confirmed effort.
Writes that fail before atomic replacement preserve the previous tier.
A connection or durability failure after replacement can leave the new tier visible; reopen the picker before retrying.
Cancelling an already-submitted save does not undo it.
Shared saves require a DSH profile with a resolved shared home and a filesystem that supports private POSIX permissions and directory synchronization.
Windows interactive persistence is unsupported; configured defaults and headless flags remain usable when no shared store exists.
Unreadable or malformed records block tier reads rather than silently restoring paid defaults; repair or remove the affected record.
With footer-hint support, explicit Auto and Fast appear beside effort, for example `(high · Fast)`.
Standard and provider-default selections stay hidden.
Provider default adds no `service_tier` field to normal requests.
Existing caller options and payload hooks remain unchanged.

## Provider sign-in

Sign in from the profile you are already using. The plugin registers a command in the harness command palette.
In additive mode, it offers providers with an installed interactive login.
In managed mode, it offers only the routes and authentication methods selected by `catalog`.

```text
/dsh-provider-extra-login [<id> [oauth|key] | status]
```

Omit the ID to pick a provider. Set `loginCommandName` to rename the command.
Set `loginCommandEnabled: false` to disable it in either mode.
The command needs a command registry and a session UI to ask sign-in questions.

Managed IDs are exactly the `Config.catalog` route IDs, shown with their configured names.
Additive IDs remain installed source provider IDs, including `opencode-go` when its configured route is aliased.
With no method word, the command uses the only available method, or OAuth first when both are available.
Use `oauth` or `key` to select a method explicitly.
A managed `apiKeyRef` route offers only key entry, including XAI.

Managed sign-in writes the configured credential reference or source record.
It never declares routes or changes Config, defaults, settings, or membership.
Additive sign-in can declare an undeclared provider in `llm-pi-ai` settings.
Credentials serve the next request without a restart.

Missing or read-only credential stores refuse sign-in before any secret or OAuth prompt.
API-key entry uses a secret-marked question and verifies the pending key before storage.
A zero-model key route fails with `cannot verify this API key: no models are available for provider <route-id>`.
That failure stores nothing. Success requires a readback from the effective credential store.

Managed status prints `API key <ref> (not set|set from <source>)` for reference-backed routes.
It never substitutes a provider record for an unresolved reference.
Source-record mode reports `not signed in` or `signed in (api_key|oauth)` from `llm-pi-ai:<credentialProvider>`.
Status and OAuth persistence do not check endpoint availability or account entitlement.

Without a command palette — a headless composition, or a sign-in for a server you are not attached to — use the shipped bin instead. It signs into the Codex route only, and needs the same `DSH_HOME` as the harness plus a profile that has booted at least once, because that is what installs the tree the bin resolves the harness packages through:

```sh
"$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/node_modules/.bin/dsh-provider-extra-login"
# If the server uses a non-default credentials file:
"$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/node_modules/.bin/dsh-provider-extra-login" --credentials-path /absolute/path/to/.credentials.yaml
```

From a source checkout, `pnpm codex:login` runs the same entry point through the TypeScript loader.

Choose device-code login for a headless host or browser login for a desktop. Follow the URL and prompts printed by pi-ai. The browser callback uses `localhost:1455`. The prompt also accepts a pasted redirect URL.

The grant is stored in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` by default. Writes use the harness document lock, and the running adapter reads the grant on the next request. Never commit the grant or include it in a bug report. Renaming `codexRouteId` changes the credential address, so keep the default unless a separate grant is intentional. Set `codexEnabled: false` to disable this route.

## Development and verification

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run check
pnpm audit --audit-level high
```

`check` runs type checking, source tests, the harness matrix guard, the build, integration tests, release guards, and the package smoke. `node tools/harness-matrix.mjs` reads the declared range, the verified releases, and what every harness package declares, and fails when the three disagree; `pnpm run matrix` is the same check.
Package checks reject non-synthetic catalog/model declarations in shipped configuration and documentation.
Development setup tests use synthetic credentials-free profiles; the setup helper stays outside the npm package. The plain-Node smoke test mounts both compiled routes in the real Cordis/LLM runtime. Two CLI tests exercise add, repeated add, profile overrides, and remove in disposable web/TUI profiles; they drive the registry CLI this repository develops against (`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.3`), so no harness checkout is needed.

Tests use a local mock gateway or seeded grants. They require no API key, OAuth login, or paid provider requests.

CI installs from the registry with read-only permissions and no account credentials, verifies dependency signatures and attestations, and runs the same checks. New dependency releases must be at least seven days old, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` limits which lifecycle scripts may run; a verified harness release is published inside that window, so only the exact versions it resolves are exempted, and only until they mature (see [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md#harness-matrix)).

The package smoke test does not prove a real account can authenticate or a remote provider is available. To verify those, install a candidate into a profile built on the supported harness line and send one message through each configured route.

Before sending a pull request, run the checks and describe the behavior changed. Report security problems privately to the repository maintainer, not in public issues. Remove keys, grants, conversation content, and machine-specific paths from shared logs.

## Releasing

Published artefacts carry a provenance attestation, which only a CI provider can issue, so releases ship from the tag workflow rather than a laptop.

1. Bump `version` in `package.json`, land it on `main` through a reviewed PR, and wait for CI to pass on the merged SHA.
2. Tag that SHA with a signed tag and push it. The tag ruleset admits repository admins only.
3. [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) re-runs the checks and the package smoke; the publish job then publishes automatically with OIDC trusted publishing and automatic provenance. Only an admin can push a `v*` tag, so the signed tag push is the release approval.

The workflow stores no npm token: the registry trusts `release.yml` on the `npm-release` environment, and [`scripts/npm/release.py`](scripts/npm/release.py) creates both the environment and that trust. The full runbook is [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md).

## License

MIT

## Git hooks

Checks run in tracked local Git hooks instead of push/PR CI. Run `scripts/setup-hooks` once after cloning; it points this clone's `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. Each hook runs the generic checks first (sign-off and commit message format, a gitleaks secret scan, and signed, signed-off commits on push), then this repository's checks in `.githooks/<hook>.d/` in name order. Install [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) first. Every check must pass before you push; never use `--no-verify`. Pre-push checks test exactly each pushed commit: in place only when it is the clean, unmodified checkout, otherwise in a temporary worktree of that commit.

This repository's checks:

- `pre-commit`: staged whitespace and conflict-marker check.
- `pre-push`: `npm audit signatures`, `pnpm run check`, `pnpm audit --audit-level high`.

# DeepSeek Usage

> DeepSeek 官方账单 + 本地 DSH 会话日志，两种口径的 Token / 用量看板 —— DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件。
> 点侧边栏「用量」弹出居中大弹窗：默认走官方账号（不登录、不落盘凭据），可切到本地聚合看 DSH 实际跑了多少。

---

## 界面预览

![在 DSH 中打开用量面板](assets/screenshots/overview.png)

| 用量趋势 | 用量日历 |
| --- | --- |
| ![用量趋势](assets/screenshots/usage-trend.png) | ![用量日历](assets/screenshots/calendar.png) |
| ![本地 AI 聚合](assets/screenshots/local-aggregation.png) | ![侧边栏标签](assets/screenshots/sidebar-settings.png) |

「各模型消费金额」有两个维度，图表右上角随时切换：「趋势」随时间展示金额，粒度跟随所选区间（当天按小时、跨天按天）；「综合」是所选区间内各模型金额的合计排行，条末直接标注金额与 Token 用量。下图是「近 7 天 + 综合」：

![各模型消费金额：趋势 / 综合两种维度](assets/screenshots/model-spend.png)

## 它是什么

DeepSeek Usage 把用量数据搬进 DSH，写代码间隙瞄一眼就知道今天烧了多少、余额还剩多少、官方账单和本地日志差多少。

- **总额**：充值余额、累计消费（官方账单口径）。
- **用量趋势**：所选范围内的消费金额、API 请求次数、Token 消耗，各模型 Token 堆叠柱状图，
  以及请求次数 / Tokens 两张走势图。
- **本地 AI 聚合**：直接读 DSH 会话日志里 provider 上报的 `usage`，按天/小时折叠；
  默认包含本机所有 Provider（DeepSeek、中转、OpenAI/Codex 等），不再有
  「DeepSeek 官方 / 全部 Provider」切换。数据源选择会持久化，侧边栏指标
  跟随当前数据源；本地模式不显示约等号，金额注明按当前费率估算（日志覆盖可能不完整，
  不声称与账单等价），费率可在面板里按模型增改；侧栏标签可直接拖拽排序，也可上传图标；
  余额仍读取官方账户余额，和本地日志范围无关。
- **本地费用估算**：内置 139 个主流模型的 USD 快照（覆盖 15 家供应商，含小米 MiMo、阶跃星辰 Step、xAI Grok、Cohere），缓存命中 / 未命中输入 / 缓存写入 / 输出四个桶分别计价，不按时段切换；面板内可按模型编辑单价、删除或恢复模型；删除默认模型按未计价处理，本地金额按 USD→CNY 汇率折算，汇率默认 6.7，可在「显示设置 → 定价」直接修改。未定价模型显示「暂无费率」，不按 0 元计入。
- **用量日历**：当月每日 Token 热力图，5 级深浅，可翻月。
- **筛选**：时间范围（今天 / 昨天 / 近 7 天 / 近 30 天 / 本月 / 上月）、模型多选。

今日数据按小时展示（和官方用量页同源：`usage/by_api_key` + 本地时区桶）；样式已固化在 `src/panel.css`，类名使用 `d-` 前缀、令牌使用 `--d-` 前缀，全部规则收在 `.d-usage` 作用域，不污染宿主。

## 数据从哪来（不需要登录）

插件**没有登录表单、不接收 token、不落盘凭据**。每次取数时按需读一次宿主的凭据记录：

```
records["deepseek-account-platform/default"].payload.token   // kind: "grant"
```

再带 `x-dsh-auth-token` 头调官方平台的内部接口（抓包确认，非公开 API）：

| 用途 | 端点 |
| --- | --- |
| 余额 / 累计消费 | `GET /api/v0/users/get_user_summary` |
| 用量明细（逐日逐模型） | `GET /api/v0/usage/amount?month=&year=` |
| 费用明细 | `GET /api/v0/usage/cost?month=&year=` |

所以在 DSH 里登录账号 = 这里有数据；在 DSH 里退出账号 = 这里显示「未检测到 DeepSeek 账号」。
上游请求统一带浏览器 UA 与 `x-app-version`，否则平台会回 429。

## 本地聚合（不需要 tokenizer）

本地模式通过宿主可选的 `sessionPersistence` 服务读会话日志，不自己解压 zstd、不建 SQLite、
不依赖 TokenLedger：

```text
persistence.list()                    # 每个会话的 header + revision + sizeBytes
persistence.open(id, 'read')          # 只读句柄，不取得写所有权
handle.read(0)                        # 全部事件
handle.close()
```

折叠口径直接采用 DSH 的 provider-reported usage：

- 四桶互斥：`cacheReadTokens` → 命中、`inputTokens` → 未命中、
  `cacheWriteTokens` → 缓存写入、`outputTokens` → 输出；`reasoningTokens` 是输出子集，不重复加。
- 同一 `(turn, step)` 的最终 `assistant/message` **替换** chunk 样本，不累加。
- Provider/model 取 `message.source`，缺失时回退最近一次 `request/header`，再缺失记 `unknown`。
- 只缓存折叠结果，不保留事件；`revision` 未变不重读；30s TTL、并发去重。

本地看到的不是官方账单的全集：官方包含所有客户端/机器，本地只含本机 DSH 会话；
本地还会包含中转/API Key 路由，也会因日志清理而缺失历史。所以对账条同时显示覆盖率和 caveat，
不假装两边 1:1。

## 安装

### DSH 桌面 App（官方客户端）

桌面 App 的 `desktop` profile 由 Electron 独占，**不能**用 `dsh plugin --profile desktop` 安装（会报 `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`）。

在 App 内操作：

1. 打开 **设置 → 插件**
2. 点右上角的 **+ / Add plugin**
3. 输入 npm 包名 `deepseek-usage`；本地开发可填本仓库的绝对路径
   （如 `/Users/you/IdeaProjects/DeepSeek-Usage`，按 `link:` 处理，改代码后刷新即可）
4. 安装完成后完全退出并重开 DSH（⌘Q）

### Web 版 / CLI

先确认 `dsh` 命令可用（DSH 桌面 App 不自带 CLI）：

```bash
dsh --version
```

没有的话，安装与 App 同版本的 CLI（把版本号换成你的 App 版本）：

```bash
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.3
```

然后按实际使用的 profile 安装（Web 版是 `web`）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add deepseek-usage
```

从源码安装（开发调试）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:sdiwenchen-lang/DeepSeek-Usage
```

装好后**重启 DSH** 生效：客户端 bundle 在启动时一次性加载。侧边栏会多出一枚
「DeepSeek Usage · 用量」按钮，点开即是面板。

> 刚启动的那一屏可能还没有第三方插件的入口：桌面端窗口先于宿主插件图加载，客户端会
> 因 “Host release changed” 暂停插件更新。**刷新一次页面（⌘R）**即可看到入口，之后一直保留。`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向
`cordis.patch.yml`，宿主加载 bundle 时自动应用补丁。

### 可配置项（都有默认值，可不写）

```yaml
- id: deepseek-usage-panel
  name: deepseek-usage
  config:
    xAppVersion: "0.1.0"                # 发给上游的 x-app-version
    requestTimeoutMs: 10000             # 单次上游请求超时
    cacheTtlMs: 600000                  # 缓存 TTL（10 分钟）
    lookbackMonths: 24                  # 月份回看上限（覆盖整年）
    retryBackoffMs:                     # 429 / 5xx 退避序列
      - 1000
      - 2000
      - 4000
    local:
      sweepTtlMs: 30000                 # 本地会话日志扫描 TTL
      maxSessions: 5000                 # 单次扫描上限
      officialProviders:                # 算作「官方计费路由」的 provider
        - deepseek-official
        - deepseek-account
        - deepseek
      pricing:                          # 可选：本地费用估算
        enabled: true
        # usdToCny: 自定义汇率；留空/0 使用内置默认 6.7
        # models:                       # USD / 百万 Tokens，四项缺一不可
        #   custom-model:
        #     input: 1
        #     output: 4
        #     cacheRead: 0.1
        #     cacheWrite: 1.25
```

默认费率来自 `src/pricing.snapshot.json`，快照日期 2026-10-30，共 139 个模型，覆盖 15 家供应商：Anthropic、OpenAI、Google、DeepSeek、xAI Grok、通义千问、Kimi、智谱 GLM、MiniMax、豆包、腾讯混元、Mistral（含 Devstral / Codestral）、Cohere、小米 MiMo、阶跃星辰 Step。保留每个家族的最新与次新版本和兼容别名，剔除预览 / 实验版本、日期别名和推理档位别名；美元兑人民币默认按内置 6.7 估算。DeepSeek 采用高峰价（USD / 百万 Tokens，命中 / 未命中 / 输出）：V4.1 Flash `0.006 / 0.30 / 1.20`，V4 Flash（旧版/兼容）`0.014 / 0.44 / 1.32`，V4 Pro `0.044 / 1.32 / 3.96`；面板不区分峰谷时段。汇率可在「显示设置 → 定价」直接点击修改；在「管理定价…」中可搜索、编辑或添加模型，可勾选行批量删除或点行尾垃圾桶删除；删除默认模型会将其从定价列表隐藏并按未计价处理，工具栏可恢复默认费率与全部模型；浏览器只保存 USD 稀疏覆盖和本地隐藏列表。旧人民币峰谷配置保留但不直接迁移。

公式为 `(未命中输入×input + 输出×output + 缓存命中×cacheRead + 缓存写入×cacheWrite) / 1,000,000` 美元，再按内置 6.7 的汇率换算为人民币。「消费金额」卡只显示人民币金额，点击不跳转。未知模型不当免费；空/未来用量为零。部分已定价的金额仅代表已覆盖部分，响应标记 `complete: false` 和 `unpricedModels`。修改费率会重算已缓存 Token，不重读未变化日志。

## 插件自有端点

全部只监听回环地址，并做双重校验（peer socket 必须是 `127.0.0.1` / `::1`，Host 头也必须是回环），
任一不满足返回 403。

| 端点 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/pricing` | 有效四通道 USD 费率、生效汇率与快照元信息 |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/status` | 数据源状态：是否检测到账号、数据源引用、是否降级 |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/summary?year=&month=` | 余额 + 指定月份逐日逐模型用量与汇总（日历页数据） |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/official?range=today\|yesterday\|last7\|last30\|thisMonth\|lastMonth` | 官方用量；也接受 `from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&tz=`（最多 800 天）。按自然月精确分片，保留首尾部分月份，未来日期补零且不请求上游 |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/local?range=…&scope=all\|deepseek&tz=&rates=` | 本地会话日志的逐日/逐小时 Token、模型、Provider、缓存命中率、coverage 与 `cost` / `costMeta`（当前费率估算）；默认 `scope=all`，`rates` 可覆盖费率，`hidden` 列表按未计价处理；也接受 `from=&to=` 自定义范围 |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/reconcile?range=…&scope=…` | 同一范围官方 vs 本地：覆盖率、差额、逐日/逐小时对账；官方未登录或本地不可用时降级一侧 |
| `GET /api/deepseek-usage/panel.css` | 面板样式表（约 105KB，独立下发，见「体积预算」） |

## 代码结构

```
DeepSeek-Usage/
├── src/
│   ├── index.js        # Cordis 入口：name / inject / optional / apply，装配依赖、注册命令
│   ├── http.js         # 回环端点、loopback 栅栏、summary/official/local/reconcile 聚合与缓存
│   ├── apiclient.js    # 唯一允许出现 platform.deepseek.com 的地方：端点、鉴权头、字段映射、重试
│   ├── account.js      # 只读宿主 credentials 里的 DeepSeek 账号（60s 缓存、并发去重）
│   ├── cache.js        # TTL + in-flight 去重
│   ├── local-fold.js   # 纯折叠：usage 事件 → 小时/route 桶；同 (turn, step) 替换
│   ├── local.js        # 本地数据源：sessionPersistence 扫描、revision 缓存、范围聚合
│   ├── pricing.js      # 四通道 USD 费率、显式 FX、缓存分析与费用覆盖率
│   ├── pricing.snapshot.json # 139 个主流模型离线默认费率
│   ├── reconcile.js    # 官方 vs 本地对账 payload
│   ├── client.js       # 浏览器半边：__ModuleLoader__ bundle，React 组件与图表（纯 SVG）
│   └── panel.css       # 面板样式（由 /panel.css 下发）
├── cordis.patch.yml    # bundle 补丁（安装入口）
└── package.json
```

服务端是纯 Node 标准库 + 宿主注入的 `credentials` / `sessionPersistence`，无运行时依赖、无构建步骤；
前端 bundle 手写 `__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`，React 由宿主作为 peer 提供。

## 开发检查

```bash
npm test               # 离线 mock API、计价、本地聚合与客户端回归
npm run bundle:check   # 客户端 bundle 体积上限 110KB（112640B）
```

几个非显然、改代码前必须知道的约束：

- **客户端 bundle 只能导出 `apply` / `inject`**。导出 `default` 会让宿主 fiber 卡在 loading，整个 web 启动失败。
- **bundle 上限 110KB**，而面板样式有 ~105KB。所以样式走 `/api/deepseek-usage/panel.css` 单独下发，
  客户端只注入一个 `<link>`；把 CSS 塞回 `client.js` 会直接超限。
- **`inject` 里只声明真用到的服务**：`credentials` 必须；`webServer` / `httpServer` / `commands` /
  `sessionPersistence` 是可选的，用 `ctx.get()` 探测——Cordis 4 下直接读 `ctx.commands` 会抛错。
  `sessionPersistence` 缺失时 `/local` 返回 503，官方模式不受影响。
- **本地聚合不要在插件里解压 zstd**：会话日志是多 frame 追加，`zlib.zstdDecompressSync` 只读第一帧；
  一律走宿主句柄的 `read(0)`。
- **上游字段名会变**，映射集中在 `apiclient.js` 的 `FIELD_MAP`，改一处即可。

## 打包（本地分发包）

没有构建步骤：服务端只用 Node 标准库，前端 `client.js` 手写 `__ModuleLoader__` bundle，
所以「打包」就是 `npm pack`，产出物可直接装进 App 或发给别人。

```bash
npm run bundle:check     # 先过体积门禁（客户端 bundle ≤ 110 KiB，超了会被挡下）
npm pack                 # 产出 deepseek-usage-<version>.tgz
npm pack --dry-run       # 只看会进包的文件清单，不落盘
```

`package.json` 的 `files` 决定包内内容：`src/`、`cordis.patch.yml`、`README.md`、
`CHANGELOG.md`、`LICENSE`。**`cordis.patch.yml` 是安装入口**（`dsh.bundle.patch` 指向它），
漏掉它包能装、但 UI 不会出现任何入口。

装进桌面 App：

1. **设置 → 插件 → + / Add plugin**
2. 选 **本地压缩包**，填 `.tgz` 绝对路径；或选 **本地目录**，填仓库根目录
   （按 `link:` 处理，改完代码刷新页面就生效，适合反复调试）
3. 装完 ⌘Q 完全退出再打开，刷新一次（⌘R）能看到侧边栏入口

CLI（Web 版 profile）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./deepseek-usage-0.1.4.tgz
dsh plugin --profile web remove deepseek-usage
```

桌面端的 `desktop` profile 由 Electron 独占，**不能**用 `dsh plugin --profile desktop`
装（报 `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`），
只能在 App 页面里操作。另外 pnpm 11 默认有 24 小时隔离期
（`minimumReleaseAge=1440`），从 npm 装**刚发布**的版本会被 `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION`
挡住，等满 24 小时或改用本地 `.tgz` / 目录安装。

发版时同时更新 `CHANGELOG.md` 与 `package.json` 的版本号，并在 GitHub 上用同名
tag 建 Release——正文就是插件市场「更新内容」里显示的版本说明。

## 体积与性能预算

| 项 | 预算 | 实测 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 客户端 bundle | ≤ 112640B | 106324B（本次验证） |
| 面板样式 | 独立下发 | ~105KB |
| 侧边栏摘要 | 每 120 秒刷新当前数据源 | 同费率口径 |
| 图表渲染 | 纯 SVG，≤ 5ms | 满足 |
| 本地 126 个会话首次折叠 | < 5s | ~2.3s |
| 本地增量折叠 | 只重读 revision 变化的会话 | 满足 |

## 安全与隐私

- 凭据只经宿主 credentials 服务按引用读取，**不写文件、不下发浏览器、不进日志**。
- token 只出现在 `x-dsh-auth-token` 请求头，不进 URL。
- 自有端点仅回环，`screenRequest` 双校验 peer socket 与 Host。
- 面板按打开、范围切换和手动刷新取数；侧边栏每 120 秒更新摘要。官方月度分片有 TTL 与 in-flight 去重，纯未来范围不读取账号或调用上游。

## 已知限制

- 依赖 platform.deepseek.com 的内部接口，官方无承诺，接口变动需改 `apiclient.js`。
- 只覆盖 platform 账号（即 DSH 已登录的那个），API Key 用量不在范围内。
- 热力图固定当月，跨年回看以月为单位。

## License

MIT，见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。

Read-only HTTP admission checks both loopback peer socket and Host; upstream account grants are read through host credentials. Local logs and account usage are sensitive, and bundled model prices/exchange rates are estimates not verified current prices. No install lifecycle hook is declared. # 插件备份

> 插件显示名：插件备份 / Plugin Backup · 包名 / 仓库：`dsh-plugins-git-sync` · [English](README_EN.md)

用你自己的 **Git 仓库**备份、恢复，并在多台设备之间同步 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件与配置**。

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugins-git-sync.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugins-git-sync)
[![CI](https://github.com/songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

![插件备份初始配置](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync/main/docs/images/settings-config.png)

*初始状态：填写 Git 仓库地址后即可开始备份；设备名称仅作示例。*

换电脑、重装 DSH 时，不用再一个个回忆装了什么插件、什么版本、配置怎么设：把插件清单推到一个私有 Git 仓库，另一台设备同步下来即可。备份内容是普通 JSON，能用 Git 工具直接查看、对比和回滚。

## 能做什么

- **备份 / 恢复**：把本机用户安装的插件（版本、启用状态、配置）推到仓库；换设备时按仓库清单装回来。
- **双向同步**：本机改动上传、仓库改动下载；两边都改时停下来让你选择，不自动裁决。
- **冲突处理**：保留本机 / 使用仓库 / 跳过，也可以手动合并配置。
- **历史回滚**：选择任意一次提交，把本机恢复到当时的状态。
- **自动同步**：打开客户端、插件安装/更新/卸载时自动同步；**没有定时器**。
- **Agent 工具**：6 个工具，让 Agent 直接查看状态、备份、恢复、同步、检查差异、查历史。
- **安全**：不读取也不上传 Token、密码、私钥；只同步白名单配置；不强制推送；改本机前先做快照。

同步对象仅限**用户后装的第三方插件**。DSH 内置插件、加载器内部条目（`cordis:*`）和本插件自身都不会被备份。

## 界面

设置 →「**插件备份**」（英文界面为 Plugin Backup）。插件页（侧边栏「插件」）也可以显示一个「备份」标签，内容相同。

![同步状态与自动同步](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync/main/docs/images/settings-status.png)

*同步状态、数量磁贴与自动同步开关在同一页；未配置仓库时不会后台同步。*

- **仓库配置**：填 Git 地址，自动识别 HTTPS / SSH / 本地路径并显示对应认证方式；已配置的设备默认折叠。
- **操作**：`同步`、`检查差异`；`备份到 Git`、`从 Git 恢复`收在「更多操作」里。
  - 点「同步」时，**没有冲突或删除/覆盖步骤就直接执行**，不再二次确认。
  - 有冲突或破坏性步骤时才弹预览确认。
- **同步状态**：状态徽标、数量磁贴（本地/仓库/待上传/待下载/冲突）与设备、分支、提交等元数据，与操作在同一个卡片内。
- **自动同步**：默认折叠，只显示开关状态与当前触发摘要；点「配置」可改启动延迟和触发条件。
- **插件列表**：默认折叠；展开后支持筛选、分页（默认每页 10 个，可选 5/10/20/50/100）与单插件同步开关。
- **历史记录**：按时间列出提交，可一键恢复；长说明单行省略。

## 安装

### 从 npm 安装（推荐）

已发布到 npm：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugins-git-sync@latest
```

或在 DSH 插件管理器 / Agent 的 `plugin_manager.install_bundle` 中使用：

```
dsh-plugins-git-sync
```

更新：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-plugins-git-sync@latest
```

### 从 GitHub 源码安装（备选）

```
git+ssh://git@github.com:songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync.git
```

HTTPS 形式：`https://github.com/songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync.git`

仓库已提交构建产物 `lib/`，使用 pnpm 的插件管理器无需额外构建即可加载。安装后重启 DSH 或刷新页面。

### 本地开发安装

```bash
git clone https://github.com/songni370/dsh-plugins-git-sync.git
cd dsh-plugins-git-sync
npm ci
npm run build          # 生成 lib/（宿主半 + lib/client.js 浏览器半）
```

然后用 `plugin_manager` 的 `install_bundle`，spec 传该目录的绝对路径。链接目录方式下，改代码后需要重新 `npm run build` 并重启/刷新。

## 快速开始

1. 在 GitHub / GitLab 等建一个**私有空仓库**（建议不要勾选自动生成 README）。
2. 打开 设置 →「插件备份」，填仓库地址：
   - **HTTPS**：选择 Git 凭据助手，或选「HTTPS 令牌」并填写保存令牌的**环境变量名**（Token 值放在环境变量里，不写进插件配置）。
   - **SSH**：使用系统 SSH Agent / `~/.ssh` 密钥，无需额外填写。
3. 点「测试连接」→ 保存。
4. 点「同步」，第一次会生成初始备份并推送。
5. 第二台设备：安装本插件 → 填同一个仓库与认证方式 → 保存 → 点「同步」或「从 Git 恢复」。

每个 DSH Profile 需要分别安装、分别同步；仓库里按 `profiles/<profile>/` 分开存放，互不覆盖。

## 同步是怎么判断的

本机保存了一份「上次与仓库一致」的**基线（base）**，每次同步比较 `base / 本机 / 仓库` 三方：

| 情况 | 处理 |
| --- | --- |
| 只有本机变了 | 推送到仓库 |
| 只有仓库变了 | 应用到本机（安装/升级/降级/启停/恢复配置） |
| 两边都没变 | 跳过 |
| 两边都变且结果相同 | 跳过 |
| 两边都变且不同，或一边删除一边修改 | 冲突，停下来等你选择 |

- 删除插件属于破坏性操作，默认不会自动执行。
- 改本机前会创建本机快照；失败时尽量回滚配置与启停状态。
- 推送被其他设备抢先时会重新拉取、重算、重试，**不会 force push**。
- 没有需要更改的内容时不会产生空提交。

## 自动同步

默认关闭。开启后由事件触发，**不按定时器运行**：

- **打开客户端**：可配置延迟（默认 15 秒；低于 5 秒会提示可能与 DSH 启动时的插件安装冲突）。
- **插件变更**：安装 / 更新 / 卸载后，防抖约 10 秒触发一次。

自动运行遇到冲突或破坏性计划会暂停并记录日志，等待手动处理，不会弹窗、不会静默删除。

## Agent 工具

工具名沿用 `dsh_git_plugin_*`（保持对既有提示词的兼容）：

| 工具 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh_git_plugin_status` | 查看状态、差异数量、最近错误 |
| `dsh_git_plugin_backup` | 备份到仓库 |
| `dsh_git_plugin_restore` | 从仓库/历史提交恢复 |
| `dsh_git_plugin_sync` | 双向同步 |
| `dsh_git_plugin_diff` | 只读差异预览 |
| `dsh_git_plugin_history` | 查看历史提交与快照 |

破坏性操作需要两阶段确认：先预览，再带 `confirm: true` 执行。

## 安全与限制

- 不收集、不上传 Token、密码、私钥、Cookie；HTTPS 只保存环境变量名。
- 不写机器绝对路径；配置按白名单过滤后才写入仓库。
- 恢复默认**不删除**仓库中没有的本机插件；远端删除只给警告。
- 只同步当前客户端对应的 Profile；其他 Profile 需单独安装、单独同步。
- 本地开发插件（无 npm 安装来源）可以记录，但其他设备无法自动安装。
- 只同步版本/启停/配置，不负责查最新版本或代替插件市场升级。

## 数据位置

默认在 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugins-git-sync/`（配置、状态、日志、工作副本、快照）。

从旧版本升级时，如果新目录不存在而旧目录 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-git-plugin-sync/` 存在，会继续使用旧目录，不会丢配置。卸载插件时不会自动删除该目录。

## 开发

```bash
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm test        # 单元 + 集成 + 浏览器半渲染测试
npm pack        # 预览发布内容
```

源码结构：

- `src/`：宿主半（扫描、Git、同步引擎、HTTP 路由、Agent 工具）
- `client/src/`：设置页浏览器半
- `tests/`：单元、双设备集成（真实临时 Git 仓库）、jsdom 渲染测试
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` · `docs/SECURITY.md` · `docs/PUBLISHING.md`

## 许可证

[MIT](LICENSE)

# dsh-live2d-theme

给 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web GUI 加背景自定义 + 右下角 Q版 Live2D 看板娘。

- **背景**：主色 / 文字色 / 渐变 / 背景图，半透明毛玻璃面板，侧边栏和对话区一起透出。
- **看板娘**：Q版 Live2D（内置 HK416、Pio），支持眼神跟随、点击随机动作、拖动、缩放、隐藏、切换模型。
- **自包含**：运行时、模型、默认背景都在包内 `assets/`，装好即可用，不依赖外网 CDN。
- **可视化设置面板**：⚙ 打开，实时改配色 / 背景 / 尺寸 / 模型，保存写回配置。

## 目录结构（包内自包含）

```
dsh-live2d-theme/
├── lib/index.mjs          # 宿主半侧：静态资源 + 模型列表 + 配置/上传接口
├── client.js              # 浏览器半侧：主题 CSS + Live2D + 设置面板
├── cordis.patch.yml       # bundle 层自注册（抗 profile 重写）
├── assets/
│   ├── runtime/           # PIXI + Live2D core（见 assets/README.md 的许可说明）
│   ├── models/            # HK416、Pio
│   ├── background/bg.jpg  # 默认背景
│   └── config.json        # 默认配置
├── README.md
└── LICENSE
```

宿主默认从包内 `assets/` 提供资源；如果你想用自己机器上的目录（例如 `D:\工具\live2`），
在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里给插件加 `config: { dataDir: 'D:/工具/live2' }` 即可覆盖。

## 安装

**方式一：插件管理器（推荐，装好即用）**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:<你的用户名>/dsh-live2d-theme
```

或在 DSH 的「插件」页面里通过插件市场 / 从仓库安装。

**方式二：手动放进 profile**

1. 把本目录拷到 `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-live2d-theme/`；
2. `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dependencies` 加
   `"dsh-live2d-theme": "file:../../plugins/dsh-live2d-theme"`，
   并在 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里加 `"dsh-live2d-theme"`；
3. 跑一次 `pnpm install`（在 profile 目录），然后重启 DSH。

> 插件自己的 `cordis.patch.yml` 会在 bundle 层自注册主条目，所以 profile 的
> `cordis.patch.yml` 被应用重写也不会丢掉注册。


## 可视化设置面板（推荐）

看板娘右上角有三个小按钮：

- **⚙** 打开设置面板：实时修改主色、背景透明度、背景图、看板娘宽高、显示/隐藏，改完即时生效；
- **✥** 按住拖动，把看板娘拖到屏幕任意位置；
- **🙈** 隐藏/显示看板娘。

面板里的 **保存** 会把当前设置写回 `D:\工具\live2\config.json`（走宿主 `POST /dsh-live2d-theme/config`，重启后也不丢）；**恢复默认** 复位成本内置默认值。面板里也可以直接选一张本地图片上传，会自动存成 `background\bg.<ext>` 并设为背景。

## 手动改配置

所有外观也在 **`D:\工具\live2\config.json`** 里，改完保存 → 刷新页面即生效（不用重启应用）：

```json
{
  "accent": "#7c5cff",
  "backgroundImage": "/dsh-live2d-theme/background/bg.jpg",
  "backgroundOpacity": 0.55,
  "gradientDark": "radial-gradient(...)",
  "gradientLight": "radial-gradient(...)",
  "modelUrl": "/dsh-live2d-theme/models/HK416/model.json",
  "modelWidth": 260,
  "modelHeight": 300,
  "marginRight": 18,
  "marginBottom": 10,
  "visible": true
}
```

| 字段 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `accent` | 主强调色（链接/高亮/焦点环） |
| `backgroundImage` | 背景图 URL；默认 `/dsh-live2d-theme/background/bg.jpg`，文件不存在自动回退渐变 |
| `backgroundOpacity` | 面板不透明度 0-1，越高面板越实、背景越淡 |
| `gradientDark` / `gradientLight` | 无背景图时的深/浅渐变 |
| `modelUrl` | 看板娘模型路径 |
| `modelWidth` / `modelHeight` | 看板娘画布尺寸（px），模型按比例自适应不裁头 |
| `marginRight` / `marginBottom` | 看板娘离右下角距离 |
| `visible` | 是否默认显示 |

**换背景图**：把任意图片放到 `D:\工具\live2\background\bg.jpg`，刷新即用（也可改 `backgroundImage` 指到别的文件名/路径）。

## 换模型

**最简单**：面板里「看板娘模型」下拉框直接选，选完即时切换（会自动重新加载 PIXI 场景）。下拉列表来自 `GET /dsh-live2d-theme/models`，扫描 `D:\工具\live2\models\` 下的目录：

- 目录里有 `*.model3.json` → 识别为 Cubism 4 模型；
- 目录里有 `model.json` → 识别为 Cubism 2 模型。

当前已内置两个模型：`HK416`（Q版，Cubism 2）、`Pio`（Q版，Cubism 2）。

**手动加模型**：把模型目录整体丢进 `D:\工具\live2\models\<名字>\`，点面板里下拉框右边的 **⟳** 重新扫描即可。模型可从 https://github.com/hacxy/l2d-models 下载。

> Cubism 4 模型需要 `live2dcubismcore.min.js`——插件启动时已自动加载过，所以 Cubism 2 / 4 都能直接用。

## 卸载 / 回滚

删掉 profile 里上面第 1、2 步加的内容，重启即可完全还原；或直接删 `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-live2d-theme` 目录。

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility, license scope or repository/package licensing. MIT code with explicit own Git/tarball URLs in dsh.install, so installation identity is not held merely for an npm 404. Native host/client serve bundled assets, configuration and uploads. No versioned DSH contract was found. assets/README separates Cubism runtime licensing and explicitly says the bundled HK416/Pio third-party models are personal-use examples that must be replaced or removed before public redistribution; package-level MIT does not resolve those assets. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
